item.title: Fed's Warsh sees US resilience, mum on rate-path view
item.description: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh voiced optimism on Friday about US economic strength and surprise about how well global economies have been "hanging in there" amid continued energy shocks and tighter monetary policy to fight inflation.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder, Leika Kihara
item.content:encoded: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh voiced optimism on Friday about US economic strength and surprise about how well global economies have been "hanging in there" amid continued energy shocks and tighter monetary policy to fight inflation. He said the US and many other economies were benefiting from an "investment surge" driven by artificial intelligence but broadening to other sectors that was creating a near-term demand shock that was putting upward pressure on inflation. "I came out of meetings here yesterday and today and it's hard to be in a discussion with central bankers and not compare notes and hear the same thing about the surge in prices," Warsh said at the International Monetary Fund and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok. With inflation a "common challenge," Warsh said global central banks undertook "a synchronous tightening in monetary policy in most places around the world, and that means there's no free riders." In the US, he said, "We made very clear that we would deliver price stability, and we removed a dose of accommodation about a month ago," in a reference to the Fed's September interest-rate hike. NO PREVIEW OF RATE PATH But in keeping with his style since taking the reins as Fed chief in May, he gave no preview about whether he feels more interest-rate hikes will be needed, or when. "I don't prejudge meetings," Warsh added in the discussion with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva. "I don't believe in saying now what I might do at the meetings that we have in the balance of this year." Warsh's colleagues at the Fed have not been reticent on their rate-path views. In recent weeks nearly all said they feel more tightening is probably needed, but most wanted to see more economic data in order to assess the inflation trend, a signal that they were unlikely to deliver a second rate hike this month. Financial markets have taken those remarks on board and are betting the Fed will wait until December to raise rates. That remained true even after reports this week showed two [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"different measures"] of inflation [USN:L1N4610KT TEXT:"running higher"] than expected and heading in the wrong direction from the Fed's 2% goal. Warsh's decision to skirt the near-term policy decision altogether and stick to broader economic themes leaves intact the expectation that the Fed will not hike this month. 'BUMPY' AI PATH TO MORE WEALTH Warsh was optimistic about the impact of AI on economic growth and productivity in the medium-term, even as he said it would be a "very bumpy" path toward what he expected would be faster productivity growth in the "real economy" that would bolster wealth. "It's obviously hitting the demand side of the economy before it's going to hit the supply side of the economy," he said. "We don't know in the next 12 or 18 months its effect on employment, but if you believe like I believe, which is it will make economies and countries that put it to good use more productive, that it's going to make it so that we will have more wealth, then that has to be a very good thing." A task force convened to advise the Fed on the impact of AI on productivity and jobs will hold a "field hearing" in the San Francisco Bay Area on November 16, he said, in what will be a first public peek at the group's work. EMERGING STRONGER He said a broadening of the investment surge beyond AI was providing some resilience to US growth. "It means we've got plenty of tailwinds that are giving some strength and durability to this economy," he said. "That sort of momentum is certainly not found everywhere in the world." But the global economy, too, was "showing resilience that I'm not sure I would have predicted five or six months ago, given what's happening in geopolitics and hotspots around the world." The IMF earlier this week said that AI investment would [USN:L1N45Z01U TEXT:"keep global growth above 3%"] this year, partly offsetting the drag from oil prices that are hovering above $100 per barrel, but risks from high debt loads and a potential sharp pullback in AI investment and asset values threaten the outlook. Warsh said that central bankers meeting in Bangkok had a common vision to safeguard price stability and were taking action to back that view, which was giving "confidence to businesses and households that's so important for growth to continue." "I believe optimistically — you might think naively — at least in the United States, we're going to come out of this stronger with a more durable economy, more capable of leading the world on economic growth," Warsh said.

item.title: India's Yes Bank expects AT1 reinstatement to cut core capital ratio by 250 bps
item.description: India's Yes Bank said on Friday it expects the reinstatement of its previously written-off additional tier-1 (AT1) bonds to reduce its core capital ratio by about 250 basis points.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's Yes Bank (YESB.NS) said on Friday it expects the reinstatement of its previously written-off additional tier-1 (AT1) bonds to reduce its core capital ratio by about 250 basis points. On Thursday, the country's top court [USN:L4N4610SV TEXT:"set aside"] the bank's write-off of 84 billion rupees ($883.7 million) in additional tier-1 bonds during its 2020 rescue, dealing a blow to the lender and regulators that had defended the move. Here are some details: Capital ratios measure a bank's financial strength by comparing its capital with its risk-weighted assets, indicating its ability to withstand losses Yes Bank's tier-1 capital ratio would remain unchanged at 14% on a pro forma basis, the bank said Yes Bank said it is reviewing the ruling and its implications and will make further disclosures "in due course" Separately, S&P Global Ratings said it does not expect India’s Supreme Court ruling against Yes Bank to affect its ratings, though it would weigh on future earnings Yes Bank’s regulatory capital is adequate, with its common equity tier-1 ratio of 13.87% as of end-March 2026 able to absorb the expected 250 bps hit while staying well above the 5.5% minimum requirement, S&P said S&P expects the roughly 84 billion-rupee hit to common equity to be largely offset by the reinstatement of the bonds It said that the lender's credit profile can withstand the ruling, which addresses procedural lapses in the write-down under the 2020 rescue The ratings agency expects Yes Bank to remain adequately capitalized, with its risk-adjusted capital ratio projected to remain between 8% and 8.5% through March 2028, compared with 9% in March 2026 It was unclear whether Yes Bank would challenge the ruling, S&P said ($1 = 95.0550 Indian rupees)

item.title: Fundadores de CoreWeave protegen sus fortunas con ventas de acciones por US$3.300 millones
item.description: Los tres cofundadores han vendido US$3.300 millones en acciones desde la salida a bolsa de CoreWeave en 2025. Las operaciones les permitieron asegurar ganancias mientras el desplome de la acción y los ...
item.dc:creator: Dylan Sloan
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Tres cofundadores de CoreWeave Inc. ( CRWV ) han vendido acciones de la empresa por valor de US$3.300 millones desde la salida a bolsa del año pasado, retirando así sus ganancias en un momento en que el aumento de los riesgos crediticios y la cautela de los inversores respecto al gasto en inteligencia artificial provocan volatilidad en la cotización de la acción. Michael Intrator, Brian Venturo y Brannin McBee se incorporaron el año pasado al Índice de Multimillonarios de Bloomberg, que recoge a las 500 personas más ricas del mundo, después de que las acciones de CoreWeave se dispararan tras su salida a bolsa en marzo de 2025. Las acciones subieron un 359% desde el precio de salida hasta alcanzar su máximo tres meses después, lo que elevó el patrimonio neto de Intrator a US$11.800 millones. Ver más: La deuda de CoreWeave se desploma y reaviva los temores sobre una burbuja de la IA Dado que las acciones de la empresa han caído más del 60% desde ese máximo histórico, el trío ha vendido acciones por valor de miles de millones, incluidos US$2.400 millones solo este año. Al precio de cierre de hoy, las acciones que han vendido desde la salida a bolsa valdrían casi un tercio menos que los ingresos antes de impuestos obtenidos por la venta de las mismas. “Nuestros cofundadores siguen siendo tres de los seis principales accionistas de CoreWeave y, en conjunto, poseen aproximadamente el 20% de la empresa”, afirmó un portavoz de la empresa en un comunicado enviado por correo electrónico. “Están tomando decisiones de planificación financiera personal que cualquier fundador responsable con una participación concentrada tomaría. Todas las ventas están programadas con antelación, se han hecho públicas en su totalidad y son totalmente habituales”. Las acciones de CoreWeave se desplomaron un 15% el miércoles, antes de repuntar ligeramente el jueves. La caída se produjo cuando un indicador del riesgo crediticio de la empresa alcanzó un máximo histórico después de que McBee hablara de recurrir a capital “ilimitado” de las aseguradoras en una entrevista con el Financial Times. Tras liquidar acciones por valor de menos de US$70 millones el año pasado, Intrator ha acelerado el ritmo de sus ventas en 2026, deshaciéndose de más de US$907 millones en acciones de la empresa desde el 1 de enero, según datos recopilados por Bloomberg a partir de los documentos presentados. Esto le ha convertido en uno de los cinco mayores vendedores con información privilegiada de cualquier empresa estadounidense en cada uno de los dos últimos trimestres. Ha vendido el equivalente al 16,5% de su participación accionarial no diluida a fecha de la salida a bolsa. En términos porcentuales, McBee ha vendido aún más: sus ventas por valor de US$1.060 millones desde la salida a bolsa, incluidos US$577 millones solo este año, representan una reducción del 40,4% de su participación no diluida a fecha del debut en bolsa de la empresa. Casi el 40% del patrimonio de McBee se encuentra ahora en efectivo y equivalentes, según el índice de riqueza de Bloomberg. Ver más: CEO de Nvidia minimiza temores por la deuda de CoreWeave y sus acciones revierten pérdidas Los US$734 millones en ventas de acciones de Venturo durante el segundo trimestre le convirtieron en el segundo mayor vendedor con información privilegiada de cualquier empresa estadounidense durante ese periodo, y contribuyeron a que sus ventas totales superaran los US$1.200 millones desde el debut de CoreWeave en los mercados públicos. Ha vendido más del 35% de su participación en la salida a bolsa. A pesar de que estas ventas han protegido parte de su patrimonio neto, la caída de CoreWeave ha supuesto pérdidas significativas para cada uno de los tres multimillonarios. En conjunto, han perdido US$15.000 millones en patrimonio contable desde que la acción alcanzara su máximo histórico en junio de 2025. Incluso antes de que la empresa saliera a bolsa, los tres cofundadores ya habían obtenido millones mediante ventas previas a la OPI. Intrator, Venturo y McBee vendieron conjuntamente acciones por valor de US$488 millones a través de ofertas públicas de adquisición independientes en 2023 y 2024, según un folleto presentado ante la Comisión de Valores y Bolsa de EE.UU. item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Indonesian stocks dive 11% as MSCI weighs market reclassification

MSCI said on Friday (Oct 16) it plans to downgrade Indonesia to "standalone" status, sparking a sell-off.

People sit near an electronic board showing stock market index at the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Feb 2, 2026. (File photo: Reuters/Willy Kurniawan)

FAST

JAKARTA: Indonesian stocks plunged more than 11 per cent on Friday (Oct 16) as index compiler MSCI said it was "no longer appropriate" to maintain the country's emerging-market status, fuelling fears of an exodus of foreign investment. Indonesian equities have struggled since January when MSCI froze Indonesia in its indexes and threatened a downgrade to "frontier" status because of opacity in ownership and trading behaviour. On Friday, MSCI said reforms to address those problems have not made sufficient progress and that even a downgrade to frontier wouldn't reflect the severity of issues. "Significant concerns remain around market dysfunction," MSCI said. "Accordingly, MSCI considers Indonesia's continued classification as an emerging market no longer appropriate," it said in a statement.

Instead, it proposed a downgrade to "standalone" status, which would exclude Indonesian stocks from global indexes tracked by billions of dollars in passive investment, forcing funds that follow or are ranked against the indexes to sell. Argentina, Lebanon and Palestine are among the markets with the designation, with none in Asia, according to Bloomberg. UBS estimated a removal by MSCI could trigger about US$4 billion of passive outflows from Indonesia, with active investors potentially adding a further US$15 billion in outflow.

item.title: Modi's predicament: Gen Z pours out on India's streets as dissent surges
item.description: Analysts say the youth protests, and growing support for the opposition, form the worst crisis for Modi since he came to power in 2014, with people under 30 making up nearly one quarter of the country's 1 billion voters.
item.dc:creator: Tora Agarwala, Saurabh Sharma, Sunil Kataria
item.content:encoded: Despite tens of thousands of security personnel deployed to stop them, youth protesters in India scaled barricades last week, chanted anti-government slogans and scuffled with police officers trying to drag them away. "Long live the revolution," shouted one young man before police bundled him into a bus. Street protests in India this year are likely to be higher than at any time in the past decade, the independent Armed Conflict Location and Event Data (ACLED) Project has said, as dissent mounts against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government and Gen Z activists pour on to the streets. Analysts say the youth protests, and growing support for the opposition, form the worst crisis for Modi since he came to power in 2014, with people under 30 making up nearly one quarter of the country's 1 billion voters. But his government remains stable and the next general election is not due until 2029. "The nation has suddenly found its voice," said Yogendra Yadav, an anti-government activist who has played a leading part in the demonstrations. "I would not say this is the beginning of the end of the Modi regime, but this definitely is the beginning of a downward spiral". The government and Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party declined comment for this story. The recent protests in the capital Delhi and elsewhere were focused on demands that Election Commission chief [USN:L4N45K0DB TEXT:"Gyanesh Kumar"] resign over a [USN:L4N45K0E7 TEXT:"voter roll revision"] that activists and opposition parties say favours the BJP and has helped it win several recent state elections. The ruling BJP, the government and the Election Commission deny the accusations. The BJP says the party's wins have come from Modi's popularity and strong economic growth. But the demonstrations are also reflecting something larger: growing anger at Modi for failing to deliver jobs to millions of unemployed youth in his 12 years in power despite the surge in headline economic growth. Other issues have also fed into the anti-establishment mood, including leaks of question papers in [USN:L4N43O0C9 TEXT:"key examinations"] for jobs and education, the high number of crimes against women and the rise of billionaire businessmen alleged to have close links to Modi. Modi has a strongman image and his government has previously cracked down on pockets of dissent harshly, but that hasn't fazed the youngsters on the streets. "The fear in us is gone," said Ananya Raturi, a 21-year-old Delhi University student who was part of massive protests in the capital on Saturday. Speaking after she clung to the windscreen wipers of a bus that police were using to detain protesters, Raturi said: "We don't fear being detained or beaten up by the police. This generation enjoys it." Police have denied allegations that they beat up people at the demonstrations, saying protesters were handled according to prescribed procedures. REUTERS/Priyanshu Singh Supporters of the opposition parties join in a protest march to the Supreme Court to protest a controversial revision of voter lists that has sparked days of unrest, in New Delhi, India, October 12. REUTERS/Bhawika Chhabra Police detain Indian National Congress lawmaker Priyanka Gandhi Vadra as she lies on the ground, during a protest organized by opposition parties demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India, October 7. REUTERS/Adnan Abidi Policewomen try to stop a detained protestor escape from a bus during a protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) seeking the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner in New Delhi, India, October 10. REUTERS/Priyanshu Singh Policewomen try to stop a detained protestor to escape from a bus during a protest seeking the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, near the protest site in New Delhi, India, October 10. REUTERS/Adnan Abidi Supporters surround a bus carrying the leaders of India's opposition parties as they take part in a march to the Supreme Court in protest against a controversial revision of voter lists that has sparked days of unrest, in New Delhi, India, October 12. REUTERS/Adnan Abidi A protester is detained by security personnel during a protest seeking the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, near the protest site in New Delhi, India, October 11. REUTERS/Adnan Abidi Police and security personnel stand guard behind barricades as opposition parties march to the Supreme Court to protest a controversial revision of voter lists that has sparked days of unrest, in New Delhi, India, October 12, 2026. REUTERS/Priyanshu Singh Protesters are detained by security personnel during a protest seeking the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, October 11. REUTERS/Adnan Abidi Protesters hold each others' hands as they are detained by security personnel during a protest seeking the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, October 11. REUTERS/Priyanshu Singh Protesters react as they are detained by security personnel during a protest seeking the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, October 11. REUTERS/Adnan Abidi A member of a security force detains a protester on top of a bus during a protest seeking the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, October 13. REUTERS/Priyanshu Singh THE RISE OF THE COCKROACHES The protests have been energised by the emergence of the first nationally resonant youth-led movement of the Modi era, the [USN:L4N45W00W TEXT:"Cockroach Janta Party"], which grew from online satire into a nationwide campaign this June after India's chief justice likened the unemployed to "cockroaches". India's mainstream media is mostly pro-government, critics say, and has covered the protests sparingly. But thousands of protesters armed with mobile phones as well as independent news channels on YouTube have amplified the unrest and made Internet stars of leaders like CJP founder [USN:L1N45W01X TEXT:"Abhijeet Dipke"] and firebrand left-wing activist [USN:L4N45X011 TEXT:"Neha Bora"]. Opposition parties that were subdued under Modi's grip on power have been re-energised, with Congress Party leader Rahul Gandhi and tens of thousands of followers also on the streets. The unrest has drawn comparisons with neighbouring Bangladesh and Nepal, where youth-led protest movements brought down governments in recent years, although analysts caution that India's political landscape and Modi's popularity make such parallels imperfect. Many of the youth protesters grew up during Modi's rise to power, buoyed by promises of jobs, opportunity and cleaner governance. A decade later, many say those aspirations remain unfulfilled and they say the Hindu nationalist government appears more focused on religious issues and divisive politics against minorities, especially Muslims. Ananya Raturi, 21, reacts as she tries to stop the police bus carrying detained protesters during a protest organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), seeking the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India, October 10, 2026. REUTERS/Priyanshu Singh/File Photo The government has previously said the economy generated 168.3 million new jobs in the six years through 2024. Modi has repeatedly rejected allegations of any bias, saying his government works for all Indians. 30-year-old Gauri Seth, a medical student based in Kolkata, became a voter in 2014, the same year the Modi government came to power. Seth said the Modi government promised "a lot, but has failed to deliver." "Instead they focus on things like religious infrastructure. There are cases of violence against minorities. When anyone speaks against them, it is labelled as treason or sedition." IT'S MOSTLY ABOUT JOBS When Modi came to power, he promised the creation of millions of jobs each year. Yet, despite India's strong economic growth since then, unemployment remains at slightly above 5%, according to government data. A Reuters poll last year said that data masks the [USN:L4N3TC0XX TEXT:"severity of joblessness"], especially among the youth. Unemployment among the 367 million people in the country aged 15-29 stood at 9.9% in 2025, according to the data. Research by Azim Premji University's State of Working India 2026 report found unemployment among graduates aged 15-25 was nearly 40%, while about one in five graduates aged 25-29 remained jobless. In May, unrest erupted across the country when the government invalidated examinations for national medical colleges, a pathway to jobs for the poor and the middle class , after test papers were leaked. Rubby Singh, a 30-year-old social activist in Delhi, said repeated examination paper leaks had deepened a sense among young Indians that the system was denying them opportunities even after years of study. "This generation has been facing the brunt of not having proper education, which leads to not being able to get good opportunities," she said. Neha Bora, National President of the All India Students' Association (AISA), reacts as she is detained by police during a protest against alleged assault on female protestors and journalists by Delhi Police and demanding resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in New Delhi, India, October 4, 2026. REUTERS/Bhawika Chhabra/File Photo While national elections are not due for almost three years, the country's biggest state, Uttar Pradesh, goes to the polls early next year, which could provide a test of Modi's popularity. Analysts however remain cautious about the outcome. The BJP may not be as strong as it was a few months ago, said Rahul Verma, a fellow at the Centre for Policy Research in New Delhi. "But whether there are going to be electoral implications, it is too early to say."

item.title: Don't Give Up on Peace in the Democratic Republic of Congo
item.description: The peace deal agreed in December by the presidents of the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda, brokered by a beaming President Donald Trump, was doomed to fail. The main belligerent in the conflict, the March 23 Movement (M23) rebel group that controls the mineral-rich eastern DRC, wasn’t a signatory. And the optics were inauspicious: Trump mispronounced the names of Rwanda’s Paul Kagame and the DRC’s Felix Tshisekedi, and the pair avoided eye contact and wouldn’t shake hands.

item.title: Power, bullpen steer Brewers to NLCS sweep, first Series bid since '82
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- Their rallying cry was "Our way," and in the end, the Milwaukee Brewers plowed their way into the franchise's first World Series appearance in 44 years by doing it every way possible.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: LOS ANGELES -- Their rallying cry was "Our way," and in the end, the Milwaukee Brewers plowed their way into the franchise's first World Series appearance in 44 years by doing it every way possible. Clutch hitting, pitching and even a newly discovered power game lifted the Brewers to a four-game sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League Championship Series. Jake Bauers started the Brewers' Game 4 comeback with a two-run double and Garrett Mitchell hit a go-ahead home run to deliver a 6-4 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers on Thursday. Bauers added a bases-loaded walk to tie the game in the fifth inning as the Brewers rallied from an early four-run to become the first team to sweep the same club that swept them out of the playoffs one year prior. "They have a bunch of Hall of Famers, but we have a bunch of gamers, and the gamers won this week," Milwaukee manager Pat Murphy said at the on-field trophy presentation. Catcher William Contreras guided the Brewers' pitching staff in a bullpen game, and four pitchers held the Dodgers scoreless over the final seven innings. JoJo Romero (2-1) tossed two innings, and Aaron Ashby handled the final three frames for his second save of the postseason. Bauers was selected the Most Valuable Player of the NLCS after going 4-for-14 (.286) with one homer and six RBIs. "I can't speak for anybody else, but for me, watching the way they carried themselves on the field after sweeping us last year was a little bit eye-opening," Bauers said. "Those guys swept us, they sent us home, and you would have thought it was a handshake line at a spring training game. That's something that I carried with me. That's something that I remembered. "Yeah, it was a little bit of motivation to just say, 'We've got to keep going until there's not another game left to play.'" The Brewers will open the World Series at home on Oct. 23 against the winner of the American League Championship Series between the Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays. The Guardians hold a 2-1 lead after winning 3-2 on Thursday. Milwaukee made its only previous World Series appearance as an AL team in 1982, falling in seven games to the St. Louis Cardinals. Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani hit a three-run homer in his return to the leadoff spot but also struck out three times while playing with knee and biceps discomfort that will be addressed in the offseason. "I was grateful to spend time together as a team," Ohtani said through an interpreter. "Although we fell short, and are definitely disappointed, I want to use this as a catalyst to have a better season as a team (next year)." Dodgers starter Tyler Glasnow gave up four runs on three hits and two walks over 4 1/3 innings. He struck out six. Tanner Scott (0-1) served up Mitchell's go-ahead home run in the sixth inning. Los Angeles was trying to become the first National League club to win three consecutive World Series titles. "I can't give enough praise to the Brewers organization," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "... I think for me it never feels good to lose, but when you get beat, you can handle it a little bit better. I had a good conversation with the guys in (the Los Angeles locker room) and just told them how proud I was. "I'm not used to consolation speeches, but it was a long season. It was still a good season." The Dodgers appeared to be all business in the second inning when Andy Pages delivered a one-out RBI single and Ohtani added a towering three-run blast with two outs for a 4-0 advantage. Bauers continued his impressive series in the fourth inning with a two-run ground-rule double to cut Milwaukee's deficit in half. David Hamilton pulled the Brewers within 4-3 in the fifth inning with an RBI single, ending Glasnow's outing. Dodgers reliever Evan Phillips subsequently loaded the bases with two outs on a pair of walks. Alex Vesia replaced Phillips and walked Bauers on four pitches to tie the game. Milwaukee went up for good in the sixth at 5-4 when Mitchell, a Southern California native and UCLA alumnus, greeted Scott with a leadoff home run. The Dodgers wasted a one-out double from Kyle Tucker in the sixth inning and a leadoff double from Pages in the seventh. Another double combined with an error in the eighth put Will Smith on third base as the potential tying run with one out. Ashby then retired Tucker on a shallow fly ball and struck out Teoscar Hernandez to end the threat. Hamilton sealed the victory with a two-out home run in the ninth inning against Edwin Diaz. "You guys talk to me all the time and hear my nonsense, but the truth is these guys are a special group," Murphy said of his players. "They're together. They care about each other. I love the Dodgers. I love their players. They've got legendary players. But we came in with a group that would not be denied." --Doug Padilla, Field Level Media

item.description: [東京 １６日 ロイター] - 前場の東京株式市場で日経平均は７営業日ぶりに反発し、前営業日比１．７５％（１１２４円７３...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
午前の日経平均は7日ぶり反発、半導体中心に全面高商状 12:20 配信

東京証券取引所で2026年4月6日撮影　REUTERS/Issei Kato

[東京 １６日 ロイター] - 前場の東京株式市場で日経平均は７営業日ぶりに反発し、前営業日比１．７５％（１１２４円７３銭）高の６万５５５０円６８銭となった。前日の急落で下げ過ぎとの見方が広がり、半導体関連株を中心に幅広く買いが入って全面高商状。ただ、これまで６日続落で６０００円幅の値下がりを演じたことと比較して戻りが小さく、きょうの反騰は自律反発との指摘もある。

・米株市場でＳ＆Ｐ５００、ナスダックは小幅高にとどまったが、突っ込み警戒感もあり、日本株は朝方から買いが先行。

・大きく下げたＡＩ（人工知能）・半導体関連株が総じてしっかりとなり、市場に安心感をもたらす。

・ＴＯＰＩＸは１．８３％高の４０７２．７１ポイントで取引を終えた。東証プライム市場指数は前営業日比１．８３％高の２０９８．９４ポイントだった。プライム市場の売買代金は３兆７５１２億５３００万円だった。

・東証３３業種では、電気・ガスを除く３２業種が上昇。

個別では、キオクシアホールディングス、ソフトバンクグループなどが堅調。リクルートホールディングスが上場来高値を更新した。半面、パナソニック　ホールディングスがさえない。

・東証プライム市場の騰落数は、値上がりが１３３９銘柄（８６％）、値下がりは１７９銘柄（１１％）、変わらずは３２銘柄（２％）だった。

＜野村証券　ストラテジスト　澤田麻希氏＞

「日経平均は７営業日ぶりに反発したものの、これまでの下げを踏まえれば自律反発の域は出ない。インフレ加速も引き続き警戒される」

「前回決算シーズン前の７月もＡＩに関する不安から調整。決算発表で好実態が明らかになって反発したが、今回も同様のケースとなる可能性もある」

「過去２─３年の日経平均のＰＥＲが推移したレンジは１６─１８倍。前日は１５倍台になり、割安感が生じた格好だ」

item.title: Winger Nawaqanitawase to make decision on international future next year
item.description: Dual-code winger Mark Nawaqanitawase said on Friday he will decide on his international future next year and that he is only focused on his next move to Japanese club Wild Knights.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Dual-code winger Mark Nawaqanitawase said on Friday he will decide on his international future next year and that he is only focused on his next move to Japanese club Wild Knights. Wallabies coach Les Kiss is keen to secure Nawaqanitawase for the Rugby World Cup but the player's agent [USN:L4N45Z0F5 TEXT:"said"] this week there was no guarantee he would play for the national team again given he would also qualify for Fiji or Italy midway through next year. Nawaqanitawase responded to the speculation in a post on social media. “My only focus right now is moving to Japan in a couple of weeks and connecting with my new team at Saitama Panasonic Wild Knights," said the 26-year-old, who has Fijian and Italian heritage through his parents. “I will weigh up my options and make a decision next year on my international future." Nawaqanitawase finished up his spell with the Sydney Roosters after his tries helped them to the National Rugby League (NRL) [USN:L4N45Q016 TEXT:"title"] earlier this month and is returning to the 15-man game on a two-year deal with the Wild Knights. Kiss confirmed the winger would not join the Wallabies for November's Nations Championship tests in Europe but thought he would be back in the green and gold of Australia before next year's World Cup on home soil. "We've had a couple of chats and (we were) always waiting for the end of the year to see where he sits," Kiss told reporters. "He's had a big year, a fantastic year, hasn't he? So the conversations are being wrapped around making sure we get what's right for him. "I think there's no doubt that you know he wants to be back in the game for us, that's for sure." Kiss, himself a former rugby league winger, said Nawaqanitawase would need some time to readjust to rugby union and was not certain to come straight back into the side. "Everyone will earn their way," he said. "But if he's playing good footy, he'll be in the mix, that's for sure. "It's a different game in terms of height and how you attack the game, how you move in the game, how you defend, how the aerial game is different, so he's got a lot of things just to relearn. "Won't take him long, that's for sure." Nawaqanitawase made 11 appearances for the Wallabies before switching to the NRL, where he built a reputation as one of the game's biggest aerial threats as well as someone able to conjure up stunning tries.

item.title: インドネシア株11％急落、ＭＳＣＩ「スタンドアローン」検討で
item.description: [１６日 ロイター] - １６日のインドネシア株は１１％以上急落し、通貨ルピアも大幅に下落した。世界的な株価指数算出...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
インドネシア株11％急落、ＭＳＣＩ「スタンドアローン」検討で 12:16 配信

ジャカルタのインドネシア証券取引所で、２０２６年２月２日撮影　 REUTERS/Willy Kurniawan

[１６日 ロイター] - １６日のインドネシア株は１１％以上急落し、通貨ルピアも大幅に下落した。世界的な株価指数算出会社ＭＳＣＩがインドネシア株式市場について、もはや「エマージング（新興国）市場」ステータスに値していないと表明したことを受けた。

主要株価指数は寄り付きで８％急落し、３０分間の取引停止を招いた後も下落幅を拡大。一時１１％安と、１日の下落率としては１９９８年１月以来の大きさとなりそうな勢いだ。

今年に入ってすでに４０％近く下落しており、域内で最もパフォーマンスの悪い株式市場となっている。

ルピアは１ドル＝１万８０７０ルピアまで下落し、８月上旬以来の安値。過去最安値の１万８１９０ルピアに迫った。

ＭＳＣＩは、インドネシア株を「スタンドアローン市場」ステータスへ移行するプロセスに組み入れたと明らかにした。

item.title: Philippines hits back at Chinese envoy over 'thinly veiled threat' of force
item.description: The Philippines has chided China's ambassador for what it interpreted as a "thinly veiled threat" of force, after Beijing's envoy said his country would prevail in a confrontation between them.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Philippines has chided China's ambassador for what it interpreted as a "thinly veiled threat" of force, after Beijing's envoy said his country would prevail in a confrontation between them. Here are some details: The Philippine foreign ministry said Ambassador Jing Quan's remarks to journalists on Thursday were a "poor choice of words" and unhelpful given their complicated bilateral ties Jing had said China "may easily win" but would not use force as "we love peace" The ambassador was asked for his reaction to the Philippine defence secretary calling China a regional "troublemaker" Their comments were the latest heated exchange between China and US defence ally the Philippines, which have repeatedly sparred over disputed features in the South China Sea Asked on Friday about the ambassador's remarks, Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr said it "sounds very much like a threat" deserving of a discussion with the envoy The Chinese embassy said the ambassador had been selectively quoted and called Manila's response an "over-interpretation", adding relations were currently "at an extremely sensitive stage" China's foreign ministry said Beijing's position on improving and developing relations with Manila is clear and it hopes that the Philippine side will understand it "accurately and comprehensively” The Philippines and China have been at loggerheads for years over reefs and islands in the South China Sea located in the Philippine exclusive economic zone, with their coast guards squaring off repeatedly

item.title: Indonesia's president ready to accept foreign assistance to combat fires, foreign minister says
item.description: Indonesia's President Prabowo Subianto has agreed to accept assistance from neighbouring countries to tackle its worst forest fires in more than a decade, the country's foreign minister said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indonesia's President Prabowo Subianto has agreed to accept assistance from neighbouring countries to tackle its worst forest fires in more than a decade, the country's foreign minister said. Indonesia has come under heavy criticism after months of [USN:L6N4610Y7 TEXT:"fierce wildfires"] that have caused respiratory problems for hundreds of thousands of people and spread thick haze into neighbouring countries, leading to school closures in [USN:L6N4600NO TEXT:"Malaysia and East Timor"]. Last month, Malaysia offered to deploy three helicopters, an aircraft, and 52 personnel to help contain the fires, but there has been no follow-up since. Singapore, another country badly affected by the haze, has also said it is ready to step in to help contain the fires. "The President has already expressed his approval, and the matter is currently being discussed at the technical level within the BNPB," Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir said, according to a voice a recording shared by his ministry on Friday. BNPB is Indonesia's disaster mitigation agency. The new chief of the agency, appointed on Thursday, said he is [USN:L6N4610HK TEXT:"reviewing"] the types of assistance being offered and will decide which ones can be accelerated. The islands of Sumatra and Borneo, close to Singapore and Malaysia, have been the worst affected, with the fire able smoulder slowly beneath the surface of large stretches of peatland and re-emerge at any moment. Fire also spread to the national park of Mount Bromo in East Java, where four people involved in fighting fires were killed, the Forestry Ministry said in a statement on Friday. Two others are undergoing medical treatment for severe burns.

item.description: Spain loves bacalao — a salted cod dish that it’s shared with the world during a centuries-long enthusiasm. So I was startled to hear an apology for eating too much of the fish from a Spaniard at a culinary conference in San Sebastian. It was an aside at a talk about the natural and commercial history of gadus morhua, but it reflected guilt from a catastrophic event more than 30 years ago: Canada’s 1992 moratorium on taking Atlantic cod from its territorial waters off Labrador and Newfoundland.

FAST

BANGKOK, Oct 16 : Finance leaders of the G7 grouping agreed to hold tabletop exercises to guard against AI cyber attacks, Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said, as policymakers increasingly seek to coordinate responses to growing cyber security risks. The agreement comes after the International Monetary Fund warned this week that confidence could be undermined by an AI-enabled cyber attack on a critical service of a financial institution. "The G7 finance deputies had been discussing the idea of doing tabletop exercises on frontier AI, which was signed off at the ministerial level," Katayama told reporters on Thursday. She made the remarks after attending a meeting of finance ministers and central bank governors of the G7 advanced economies held on the sidelines of the IMF's annual gathering in Bangkok, the Thai capital.

The plan will feature simulations evolved by G7 finance authorities to test how they can respond to AI-driven cyber attacks, said a Japanese finance ministry official who attended the finance leaders' meeting. The results will test effectiveness of existing protocols and be used to revise manuals to better tackle such incidents, the official told reporters. The exercises by G7 finance ministries and central banks could include private financial institutions depending on the nature of simulations, the official added. Banking regulators globally are stepping up efforts to contain growing AI risks, Reuters reported, with some pointing to the potential for cyberattacks on banks or rogue agents undermining global financial stability. Among them is the Bank of England, which is working with banks on deep cyber-recovery options, its deputy governor said on Thursday, adding that they can no longer assume their defences are immune to AI-enabled cyberattacks.

BANGKOK, Oct 16 : World Bank President Ajay Banga on Friday said the development lender has set a goal of quintupling its critical minerals business in five years, and has identified 20 countries that it can partner with on critical minerals development projects. Banga revealed the new goal in prepared remarks to a plenary session at the International Monetary Fund and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok. "In critical minerals, we plan to quintuple our business in five years," Banga said. "This week, we launched our first country compacts with MDB partners—to build local industries and keep more jobs and value at home." The World Bank's new Metals and Minerals implementation plan is targeting $19 billion in critical minerals financing over the fiscal 2026-2030 period, compared with $3.6 billion in the fiscal 2021-2025 period.

Critical minerals development is an area where the United States, the World Bank's largest shareholder, has called for the bank to devote more financing resources. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said earlier this week that he wanted the bank to play a bigger role in enabling critical minerals mining and processing capacity through project de-risking and finance and investment in enabling infrastructure. He said this includes deep-sea mining projects. Banga did not mention deep-sea mining, but the bank's metals plan calls for a "precautionary approach" to the nascent sector, adding that any engagement and investments must be consistent with applicable bank policies. Banga reviewed the World Bank's overall increases in financing during the 2026 fiscal year that ended on June 30, including mobilizing $112 billion in private capital, a more than threefold increase from the 2022 fiscal year, before he assumed his role. Alongside lending from the World Bank's own balance sheet, this brought the group's total financing to $230 billion for fiscal 2026, he said.

Source: Reuters

item.title: 世界のＥＶ販売、9月は前年比2％減 7カ月ぶりマイナス
item.description:
Amir Orusov
[１６日 ロイター] - 英調査会社ベンチマーク・ミネラル・インテリジェンス（ＢＭＩ）が１６...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
世界のＥＶ販売、9月は前年比2％減　7カ月ぶりマイナス 11:47 配信

写真はテスラの電気自動車（ＥＶ）。２０２５年４月、フランスのパリ近郊ヴァラントンで撮影。REUTERS/Benoit Tessier

Amir Orusov

[１６日 ロイター] - 英調査会社ベンチマーク・ミネラル・インテリジェンス（ＢＭＩ）が１６日公表したデータによると、９月の世界の電気自動車（ＥＶ）需要は前年同月比２％減少し、７カ月ぶりにマイナスに転じた。欧州の販売台数は過去最高となったが、北米と中国の大幅な落ち込みを相殺するには至らなかった。

主要ＥＶ市場間の格差拡大が浮き彫りになった。欧州は旺盛な消費者需要と政策支援の恩恵を受けている一方、中国の国内市場は低迷が続き、北米では２０２５年９月末に米連邦政府のＥＶ税額控除が終了した影響が続いている。

・９月の世界のＥＶ販売台数は２１５万台に減少。一方、年初来の累計販売台数は前年同期比３％増の１５５０万台となった。

・ＢＭＩのデータマネジャー、チャールズ・レスター氏は「欧州の９月ＥＶ販売台数は約６０万台と、これまでの最高だった６月を１０％上回り、月間の過去最高を記録した」と述べた。

・北米の９月の販売台数は前年同月比４４％減と、今年最大の落ち込み。前年同月には税額控除の終了を前に販売店への駆け込み需要が膨らんでいたことが響いた。

・レスター氏は、第４・四半期からは税額控除終了後に販売が急減した時期との比較になるため、前年との比較による影響は和らぐとの見通しを示した。

・中国の販売台数は前年同月比１８％減の１１１万台となり、メーカーは輸出への依存を強めている。

item.title: Indonesian stocks sink most since 1998 on MSCI downgrade warning
item.description: Indonesian stocks suffered their steepest one-day fall in 28 years on Friday after MSCI said the country was no longer worthy of emerging market status, threatening billions of dollars in capital outflows from Southeast Asia's largest economy.
item.dc:creator: Sameer Manekar
item.content:encoded:
Indonesian stocks suffered their steepest one-day fall in 28 years on Friday after MSCI said the country was [USN:L4N46124S TEXT:"no longer worthy of "emerging market" status"], threatening billions of dollars in capital outflows from Southeast Asia's largest economy. In a surprise move on Friday, MSCI said it would put Indonesia on a path to a "standalone market" status, worse than the previously flagged "frontier" category. A downgrade would exclude Indonesian stocks from indexes tracked by global funds, potentially triggering billions of dollars in capital outflows. The Jakarta Composite Index (.JKSE) plunged as much as 11.4% to its lowest point since early November 2020, clocking its worst one-day drop since January 1998. Indonesian shares have lost nearly 40% this year, making them the world's worst-performing equity market. "Indonesia's immediate priority should be to demonstrate measurable improvements in market transparency and regulatory enforcement, rather than merely announcing additional reforms," Josua Pardede, chief economist at Bank Permata, said. Foreign investors have pulled $4.6 billion from Indonesian equities this year, as per LSEG data. UBS estimates that removal from global indexes could trigger a further $4 billion in passive outflows and about $15 billion from active investors. If downgraded, Indonesia would join Argentina, Lebanon, Palestine, and Ukraine in the standalone category, becoming the only Asia-Pacific market in the group and its largest economy, with a GDP more than twice Argentina's. On Friday, blue-chip stocks, including major lenders, miners, and energy firms, declined nearly 15%, the exchange's lower limit. The rupiah, one of the worst-performing currencies this year, weakened to 18,070 per US dollar, its lowest since late July, before paring losses to 18,000 a dollar. "Conviction has weakened and a pick-up of active fund outflows in the short-term cannot be ruled out," Citi analysts wrote, adding that their base case remains for Indonesia to retain its emerging-market classification. "Continued outflows by active funds have become likelier in our view in light of the latest MSCI downgrade warning. This would come ahead of potentially mid-single-digit billion dollars of passive fund outflows if the downgrade materializes." In East Asia, South Korean stocks (.KS11) rebounded from a 6-month closing low, but remained on track for their biggest weekly loss in 18 years following a brutal selloff on AI worries. Stocks in Taiwan (.TWII) edged higher after an over 3% decline the previous day, while its dollar weakened to late-July lows of 32.520 per US dollar, mainly pressured by equity outflows. An MSCI gauge of emerging Asia equities (.MIMS00000PUS) , dominated by chip stocks in East Asia, rose 1%, but was headed for its worst week since the start of the Middle East war. Elsewhere in Southeast Asia, Singapore stocks (.STI) added 0.5%, while those in the Philippines (.PSI) advanced more than 2%. The Philippine peso recovered from a record low hit on Thursday, last selling at 62.991 a dollar. Stocks in Malaysia (.KLSE) slipped 0.7%. Thai stock markets were closed for a holiday. Highlights: ** FACTBOX: Indonesia [USN:L6N46202Y TEXT:"suffers a series of market sentiment setbacks"] in 2026 ** Renewed policy support [USN:L4N4620FS TEXT:"lifts"] rupee from record-low brink to best week since March ** Indonesia financial regulator [USN:P8N44B049 TEXT:"pledges"] improvement after MSCI downgrade warning ** EXPLAINER: Why is the [USN:L6N4610Y7 TEXT:"haze"] so bad in Southeast Asia this year? Trump says he is talking to Russia and China about denuclearisation

Russian service members take part in a nuclear forces exercise at an unidentified location in Russia, in this still image taken from handout footage released on May 20, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Russian Defence Ministry)

FAST

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday (Oct 15) that Washington is holding talks with Moscow and Beijing aimed at denuclearising the countries with the biggest stockpiles of nuclear weapons. Russia has the most stored nuclear warheads, followed by the United States and China, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. The US outpaces Russia in the number of deployed warheads. During an interview with Newsmax, Trump said he expects China to "catch up" with the US within the next five years. "The whole thing is a shame, because I'd love to denuclearise if possible, but we're actually talking to Russia about that, and we're talking to China about that denuclearisation," Trump told the outlet. Newsmax reported that Trump had spoken with Chinese President Xi Jinping about denuclearisation. Trump's comments come months after the Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty expired earlier this year. The New START treaty signed in 2010 allowed one single extension, which was agreed by former President Joe Biden and Russian President Vladimir Putin for five years. Any new extension would require an executive decision to voluntarily extend the limits of the treaty.

Related:

FAST

WASHINGTON: New White House press secretary Katie Zacharia said on Thursday (Oct 15) she did not pass the bar exam after facing scrutiny about her legal career before becoming the top spokeswoman for US President Donald Trump. Zacharia, who joined the White House on Monday, has previously said she practised law before entering politics, and Trump had described her as an attorney. "You did not pass the bar exam, correct?" she was asked in an interview on Fox News' Hannity show late on Thursday. "Correct," she said in response to the host, Sean Hannity.

"I did not," she said when Hannity asked if she ever took the bar exam a second time.

Zacharia earned her law degree from Pepperdine University in 2011, according to the university. Nearly all licensed US lawyers first obtain a law degree, but law school graduates cannot legally practice law in the US without first being admitted to a state bar. On Tuesday during her first briefing, she took questions from just three reporters before ending the event in under 15 minutes. Her performance was criticised by some media commentators and political analysts, though Trump told reporters: "I thought she was very good." When asked about her performance by Hannity, she said: "What I feel is I really stepped up to the plate to do the press conference, Sean, with very little prep time."

item.title: ＭＳＣＩ、トルコ株式指数巡る変更凍結 格下げの可能性を警告
item.description:
Mrinmay Dey Rodrigo Campos
[１５日 ロイター] - 世界的な株価指数算出会社ＭＳＣＩは１５...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＭＳＣＩ、トルコ株式指数巡る変更凍結　格下げの可能性を警告 11:22 配信

ＭＳＣＩのロゴ。２０１７年６月撮影。REUTERS/Thomas White

Mrinmay Dey　Rodrigo Campos

[１５日 ロイター] - 世界的な株価指数算出会社ＭＳＣＩは１５日、トルコ株式指数に関する変更を凍結した。市場改革を評価するためにさらなる時間が必要だとし、２０２７年半ばまでに十分な進展が見られない場合は格下げの可能性があると警告した。

トルコの株式市場は、浮動株数の算出方法や、一部の銘柄における協調取引の疑いについて、投資家から厳しい目を向けられている。

ＭＳＣＩの決定により、トルコの「エマージング（新興国）市場」ステータスは維持されるが、将来的に「フロンティア市場」への格下げが行われた場合、「ＭＳＣＩ新興国市場指数」に連動するファンドによる売り圧力が生じる可能性がある。

ＭＳＣＩは、２０２７年６月までに十分な進展が見られない場合、トルコを新興国市場からフロンティアまたは「スタンドアローン」市場へと格下げすることについて協議を行うなど、さらなる措置を講じる可能性があると述べた。

item.title: Luke Hughes nets 2 goals in Devils' 7-1 domination of Rangers
item.description: Luke Hughes led the way with two of the New Jersey Devils' four second-period goals to help bury their rival New York Rangers 7-1 in Newark, N.J. on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Luke Hughes led the way with two of the New Jersey Devils' four second-period goals to help bury their rival New York Rangers 7-1 in Newark, N.J. on Thursday. Nico Daws stopped 18 shots in the victory, while Nico Hischier, Arseny Gritsyuk, Evan Rodrigues, Cody Glass, and Stefan Noesen all joined Hughes on the scoresheet. Timo Meier, Dougie Hamilton, Brett Pesce, Dawson Mercer, and Amadeus Lombardi all picked up a pair of assists each. Pavel Dorofeyev scored the Rangers' lone goal as they allowed more than three goals for the first time this season. Rodrigues took advantage of a tough giveaway and ripped it past Dylan Garand with 30 seconds remaining in the first period to give the Devils the lead. Hughes fired a point shot that bounced off a defender and snuck through the legs of Garand to double the Devils' advantage just 18 seconds into the middle frame. Hischier then made it 3-0 barely over four minutes into the second. After the Devils captain fired his shot wide on an odd-man rush, he stuck around and poked a rebound past the pad of an outstretched Garand. The Devils kept rolling just 31 seconds later as Gritsyuk made up for a missed breakaway by pouncing on a rebound and lighting the lamp, marking the end of Garand's night after he allowed four goals on 13 shots. Spencer Martin gave up three goals on 18 shots in relief. The youngest Hughes brother showcased his impressive skillset as he walked the blueline and cut in toward the net. He sent a shot off the far post and into the back of the net for his second goal of the night with 3:26 left in the second. Noesen buried his first goal of the season to make it 6-0 with just over seven minutes gone in the third period. Dorofeyev spoiled Daws' shutout bid with a power-play marker just over a minute later. Glass got in on the action to make it 7-1 with just over five minutes left in the contest. --Field Level Media

item.description:
Kentaro Okasaka
[東京 １６日 ロイター] - 経済産業省と財務省は１６日、中国産の二酸化チタンルチ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
日本政府、中国産の二酸化チタン顔料などの反ダンピング調査開始 10:52 配信

中国広東省深セン市の港に積まれたコンテナ。2025年10月30日撮影。REUTERS/Tingshu Wang

Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 １６日 ロイター] - 経済産業省と財務省は１６日、中国産の二酸化チタンルチル型を基にした顔料や調製品の輸入について、不当廉売（ダンピング）関税の要否に関する合同調査を開始すると発表した。原則１年以内に終了する。

両省によると、対象品は一般的に白色の微細粉末で、自動車用や高級建築用の塗料などに使用される。

日本酸化チタン工業会から８月、課税申請が財務相に提出され、関係法令に基づき検討を行い、調査を行う必要があると認められた。工業会によると、中国からの輸入価格と正常価格を比較した不当廉売差額率は５０－６０％。国内販売価格を著しく下回り、国内では中国産品を引き合いに値下げを要求されたり、製造コスト増に応じた値上げを断念せざるを得なくなったりしたとしている。

item.title: Dollar heads for weekly fall as investors gauge AI selloff impact
item.description: The US dollar was set for its first weekly fall in more than a month against the euro and the yen, as investors turned their focus to the US rate outlook while concerns about an escalation of the Iran conflict faded.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Rebaudo
item.content:encoded: The US dollar was set for its first weekly fall in more than a month against the euro and the yen, as investors turned their focus to the US rate outlook while concerns about an escalation of the Iran conflict faded. AI stocks have [USN:L6N460140 TEXT:"cratered"] this week and the [USN:L4N46112V TEXT:"stress has spread"] to parts of the credit market as investors who have crowded into bets all along the AI supply chain [USN:L4N46112V TEXT:"worry"] data centre operators might not manage to be profitable in time to pay their debts. Analysts noted that Wednesday's market moves may provide a preview of how currencies would react to a major AI-driven selloff, with the dollar falling instead of attracting safe-haven demand as investors shift towards a more dovish view of the Federal Reserve policy path. The Swiss franc again looks set to be the biggest beneficiary, thanks to its safe-haven status and expectations that, even in a lower-rates environment, Switzerland is unlikely to cut policy rates below the current zero level. It was set for a 0.61% weekly rise versus the dollar. The dollar index , which measures the US currency against six major peers, fell 0.25% to 101.77 and was set for a 0.45% weekly decline. It rose in two of the week's five sessions, including on Wednesday, as the boost from hotter-than-expected inflation data more than offset the drag from a selloff in tech stocks. The S&P 500 [USN:L6N4611C9 TEXT:"ended higher on Thursday"], springing back from early losses as investors concerned about AI stocks shifted into healthcare and consumer stocks. Wednesday’s “action revealed exactly what could threaten the US dollar and bring US yields lower in the next few months and in 2027: a reduction in the outlook for AI investment,” Thierry Wizman, global forex and rates strategist at Macquarie Group, said. “That's because it would reduce bond supply and impair US growth, all else equal,” he added. US RATES IN FOCUS US Treasury yields dropped earlier this week despite [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"hot inflation readings"] as [USN:L1N4600EO TEXT:"cautious remarks from Federal Reserve officials"] tempered October hike expectations. Markets assign an 87% probability to the Federal Reserve keeping rates unchanged later this month, according to the CME FedWatch Tool. Investors expect US President Donald Trump to steer clear of any escalation in the Middle East or Ukraine, as a broader conflict could hurt his standing ahead of the midterm elections fuelling inflation and possibly hurting the economy. The euro was up 0.14% to $1.1235 after climbing 0.56% on Thursday in its biggest daily rise in two months. It was on track for a 0.39% weekly gain. "Barring another big leg down in AI stocks and risk assets in general, expect the dollar to consolidate near recent highs," said Chris Turner, forex strategist at ING. "It is only when short-end rates break lower that the dollar is ready to drop. And we are not there yet," he added. The yen was on track for a 0.28% weekly rise after dropping for four consecutive weeks as the Iran conflict supported the greenback. It was last up 0.05% at 157.89. Higher oil prices tend to support the dollar while weighing on energy-importing currencies such as the euro and yen. [USN:L6N45A080 TEXT:"The Japanese currency tumbled"] in mid-September after a disappointing Bank of Japan policy meeting, but subsequently fell by around 0.30% a week as monetary tightening rhetoric by Japan's authorities supported the yen. Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said on Friday that the [USN:P8N44Z00F TEXT:"BoJ would continue to raise policy rates"] in line with economic and financial developments. The Australian dollar rose 0.55% to $0.6959 but was an outlier in heading for a fall of 0.3% on the dollar this week, after a surprisingly soft jobs report on Thursday had markets paring back expectations for another rise in interest rates.

item.description:
Greg Bensinger
[サンフランシスコ １５日 ロイター] - 米アマゾンは１５日、昨年買収した「Ｂｅｅ」ブ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米アマゾン、新しいＡＩ端末2機種発表　情報を聞き取り・記録 10:16 配信

アマゾンのロゴ。2025年2月11日撮影のイメージ写真。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration

Greg Bensinger

[サンフランシスコ １５日 ロイター] - 米アマゾンは１５日、昨年買収した「Ｂｅｅ」ブランドの下、１日を通して人々の情報を聞き取り・記録し、カレンダーのリマインダー機能やＡＩ（人工知能）を活用した分析結果を提供する２つの新デバイスを発表した。

「フロンティア」はブレスレット型で価格は７５ドル、「エクリプス」はマグネット式ポータブル充電器に似た形のデバイスで価格は１００ドル。エクリプスはスマートフォンに取り付けるタイプとなる。

サンフランシスコで開催された「TechCrunch Disrupt」カンファレンスで、アマゾンのデバイス担当責任者パノス・パネイ氏は「これらのデバイスはあなたの１日全体を『聞き取る』」と説明。「あなたが交わした会話を思い出させたり、やることリストを思い出させたり、他の人への約束があることを教えてくれたりする」と語った。

同社によると、ユーザーは電源を入れるタイミングを自分で決めることでプライバシーを管理でき、必要に応じて分析結果や過去の会話を削除することも可能。アマゾンは音声を保存しない。

データは１４日間保持されるが、ユーザーは月額１２ドルのサブスクリプションを支払うことで、その期間を延長できる。また、これらのデバイスはアマゾンのサブスクリプション型生成ＡＩ音声サービス「アレクサ＋（プラス）」にも接続可能だ。

item.title: Beyond the sell-off: What an MSCI downgrade threat could mean for Indonesia
item.description: Indonesian stocks suffered a massive 11 per cent decline on Friday after MSCI threatened its "emerging market status", which could prompt massive foreign selloff from the Southeast Asian economy.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Markets / News / Beyond the sell-off: What an MSCI downgrade threat could mean for Indonesia

Beyond the sell-off: What an MSCI downgrade threat could mean for Indonesia Indonesian stocks suffered a massive 11 per cent decline on Friday after MSCI threatened its "emerging market status", which could prompt massive foreign selloff from the Southeast Asian economy.

Beyond the sell-off: What an MSCI downgrade threat could mean for Indonesia

Saloni Goel New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 16 2026 | 1:54 PM IST

Listen to This Article

MSCI’s proposed downgrade of Indonesia is less about immediate passive outflows and more about the long-term cost of losing benchmark inclusion, according to analysts.   Indonesian stocks suffered a massive 11 per cent decline on Friday after MSCI threatened its "emerging market status", which could prompt massive foreign sell-off from the Southeast Asian economy.   According to a Reuters report, Jakarta Stock Exchange Composite plunged as much as 11.4 per cent to its lowest point since early November 2020, clocking its worst one-day drop since January 1998. Earlier in the day, the benchmark opened 8 per cent lower, which triggered a 30-minute trading halt.   MSCI reported that market participants had raised significant concerns regarding the investability of the Indonesian equity market, including persistent opacity in shareholding structures and suspected coordinated trading behaviour.   The index aggregator is considering moving Indonesia from Emerging Market to Standalone status, with feedback until April 30, 2027 and a decision by June 30, 2027.   What does it mean for Indonesia?     Indonesia's weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets index fell from 1.16 per cent at the end of 2025 to 0.43 per cent by September 30, and its constituents fell from 18 to 9, as MSCI froze additions and deleted names flagged under Jakarta's own concentrated-holding framework, Harshal Dasani, business head at INVasset PMS, said. At 0.43 per cent, he said, that forced passive selling runs to a few billion dollars, which is less than the market lost in Friday's session.   For the year, the index is down 39 per cent, making it one of the worst-performing emerging markets this year.   ALSO READ:  Stock Market LIVE: Sensex gains 300 pts, Nifty tops 23,100; Nifty IT rises over 3%

Justin Khoo of VT Markets said that forced selling by index-tracking funds, potentially accelerating foreign outflows, weakening the rupiah, and tightening domestic financial conditions are the immediate concerns for the market.   "An 11% plunge alone is unlikely to destabilize Indonesia's financial system. However, with the country's stock market already down nearly 40% this year, sustained foreign capital outflows could weaken market liquidity, discourage investment and further erode investor confidence," he added.   Standalone status, according to Dasani, is the index equivalent of delisting from global portfolios. This would make foreign ownership a discretionary hedge-fund decision rather than an allocation, and the cost of equity rises for years. He observed that Argentina went standalone in 2021 over capital controls and is still there.   Limited global spillover   Despite being Southeast Asia's largest economy, Indonesia is a small part of the MSCI Emerging Markets Index, suggesting limited direct global spillover.   Other ASEAN markets may benefit from portfolio reallocations, although broader regional sentiment remains vulnerable, he noted.   Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion. More From This Section

item.title: メタ、「ミューズ・スパーク」オープンウエート版公開
item.description: [１５日 ロイター] - 米メタ・プラットフォームズは１５日、コード作成や人工知能（ＡＩ）エージェント向けのＡＩモデル...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
メタ、「ミューズ・スパーク」オープンウエート版公開 10:06 配信

メタのロゴ。2025年6月12日、パリで撮影。REUTERS/Benoit Tessier/File Photo

[１５日 ロイター] - 米メタ・プラットフォームズは１５日、コード作成や人工知能（ＡＩ）エージェント向けのＡＩモデル「ミューズ・スパーク」のオープンウエート版を公開した。開発者がモデルをダウンロードし、用途に合わせて改変できる機会を広げる。

オープンウエートモデルは学習済みのパラメーターを開発者が改変できる形で提供するもので、開発元が管理する非公開モデルとは異なる。クローズドシステムに比べて低コストの選択肢を企業に提供できる。

• メタによると、ミューズ・スパークのパラメーター数は計８１６０億で、一度に使用するのは４２０億。一度に処理できる情報量を示すコンテキストウインドウは最大１００万トークンに対応する。

• アップルの「Ｍ５ウルトラ」を搭載した「Ｍａｃ Ｓｔｕｄｉｏ（マックスタジオ）」２台でローカルでの動作が可能で、一部のＡＰＩプロバイダーを通じても利用できる。

• メタのマーク・ザッカーバーグ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は、高度なＡＩが少数の企業に集中すべきではないと主張してきた。

• オープンウエートモデルは、企業が自社データを管理する裁量を広げる一方、大規模な運用には多くの計算資源や専門的な技術知識が必要になる場合がある。

• メタは８月、より小規模なオープンウエートモデル「ミューズ・グリマー」を公開した。

item.title: Fed Chair Warsh stresses price stability, offers no signals on rate outlook
item.description: The US central bank raised its key rate by 25 basis points in September, defying President Donald Trump's calls for cuts, as persistent inflation keeps further tightening on the table ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Fed Chair Warsh stresses price stability, offers no signals on rate outlook

Fed Chair Warsh stresses price stability, offers no signals on rate outlook The US central bank raised its key rate by 25 basis points in September, defying US President Donald Trump's calls for cuts, as persistent inflation keeps further tightening on the table

US Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh | Image: Bloomberg

AP Bangkok 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 16 2026 | 1:37 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said Friday he won't prejudge what the US central bank will do about interest rates at its upcoming meetings in October and December. The Fed increased its key interest rate by a quarter-point to about 3.9 per cent in September, its first increase in three years, and stubbornly elevated US inflation will likely lead it to hike that rate again in coming months to slow spending and help cool price pressures. But Warsh offered no fresh signals during a "fireside chat" with International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva at a meeting of financial leaders in Bangkok.

"At the Federal Reserve, we made very clear that we would deliver price stability, and we removed a dose of accommodation about a month ago," Warsh said. "I don't prejudge meetings. I don't believe in saying now what I might do at the meetings that we have in the balance of this year."   The Fed's September rate hike defied US President Donald Trump's repeated calls for the Fed to cut rates. The president criticised the Fed's rate-setting committee, though he still expressed support for Warsh, whom he appointed earlier this year. The global surge in prices is a key concern of central bankers and financial leaders meeting in Bangkok.

Also Read

Let exchange rate act as shock absorber: IMF on Fed hike impact on India

Fed, ECB minutes to show inflation fears as near-term rate hike bets fade

US Fed may skip October rate hike as labour market cools more than expected

Fed watchdog finds deficiencies but no misconduct in Powell-era project

Rupee settles 2 paise up at 95.89 against dollar after breaching 96 level

According to minutes released from the most recent meeting, most Fed officials expect that another interest rate increase will likely be needed this year. That would raise borrowing costs for mortgages, car loans, and credit cards over time. Warsh said the surge in investment driven by the craze for artificial intelligence is one of the factors behind higher inflation and the Fed's task force on issues related to AI will meet Nov. 16. "I'd say the advent of this new technology is probably the most consequential change to the US and the global economy in my lifetime to this point," he said.

Unlike military conflict and other shocks that are driving prices higher, Warsh said he believes AI will bring "huge benefit" to the world economy in time. For Fed economists who struggle to foresee the future using data that lags behind today's realities, AI could prove a vital tool, he said. "We torture data with old fashioned models to try to find out what's underlying inflation trends. Not so long from now, it won't be torture. We will have access at the fingertips of central banks to all the information in the world, and we'll be able to use new analytical tools to distill that data," he said.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: Oil eases but heads for weekly gain as investors focus on Middle East supply
item.description: Oil prices eased on Friday but were heading for weekly gains on uncertainty over Middle East supplies and a larger-than-expected draw from US crude stockpiles, while European diesel margins dropped following the IEA's decision to release more diesel.
item.dc:creator: Enes Tunagur
item.content:encoded: Oil prices eased on Friday but were heading for weekly gains on uncertainty over Middle East supplies and a larger-than-expected draw from US crude stockpiles, while European diesel margins dropped following the IEA's decision to release more diesel. Brent crude futures were down 47 cents, or 0.44%, at $105.45 a barrel by 0747 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down 62 cents, or 0.63%, to $97.35. WTI settled up more than 3% on Thursday after a big [USN:L6N46115T TEXT:"US crude stock draw"] on hurricane production shut-ins. For this week so far, Brent has increased 0.72%, while WTI has jumped 5.9%. "Uncertainty in the Middle East and concerns over the sustainability of oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz has the market pricing in a significant risk premium," ING analysts wrote in a note. Some kind of agreement between the US and Iran was required to provide more confidence to the market that stronger oil flows from the region would continue, they added. IRAN SAYS IT IS STEPPING UP STRIKES NEAR STRAIT OF HORMUZ Supply jitters also increased as attacks around [USN:L1N4600JW TEXT:"the Strait of Hormuz"] surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it was stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month. Total Hormuz clearance averaged 11.62 million barrels per day over the seven days to October 13, about 68% of the 17.15 million bpd baseline, said ship tracking firm Kpler. European diesel refining margins declined by nearly 2% on Friday to $78.67 a barrel, after the International Energy Agency [USN:L1N4610MY TEXT:"agreed"] on Thursday to release over 20 million barrels of diesel to the market. Those margins rose as high as $95 a barrel in September as diesel supply tightened because of wars in Ukraine and Iran. "Intensified Iranian attacks drove Gulf crude flows sharply lower," Kpler analysts said in a report on Thursday, adding that they expected a slower and more uneven Hormuz recovery in the absence of a comprehensive political deal. The Houthis [USN:L1N4600JW TEXT:"fired"] missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing two guards, while the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen detailed dozens of attacks on Saudi infrastructure in the escalating conflict. The Trump administration is considering [USN:L1N461108 TEXT:"lifting"] sanctions on some so-called shadow fleet vessels that have carried oil and petroleum products from countries such as Russia, Iran and Venezuela, in a bid to cut record global freight rates, a US official said on Wednesday. The discussions come days after President Donald Trump temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian diesel fuel, a move met with criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, European countries and some of Trump's fellow Republicans.

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
伊ウニクレディト、独コメルツ銀行の支配権獲得をＥＣＢが承認 9:52 配信

ドイツ銀行大手コメルツ銀行のロゴ。2026年3月16日、ドイツのケルンで撮影 REUTERS/Thilo Schmuelgen/File Photo

Valentina Za

[ミラノ １５日 ロイター] - イタリアの商業銀行２位ウニクレディトは１５日、４８％の株式を保有するドイツ銀行大手コメルツ銀行 の支配権獲得が欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）から承認されたと発表した。これにより、金融危機後として最大となる欧州銀行の越境買収計画がさらに前進する見通しとなった。

ウニクレディトは総額４５０億ユーロ規模の敵対的買収案を提示後、コメルツ銀行の株式を買い進めていた。ウニクレディトはコメルツ銀行に対する保有比率の３０％という閾値を超えることや、「上限なくさらに持株比率を引き上げること」をＥＣＢが承認したと説明した。

また買収提案に関連する「残りの規制上の手続きと条件」を完了後、年内に議決権の約５０％を取得し、コメルツ銀行の支配権を掌握できる見通しだという。

ウニクレディトは２年ほど前にコメルツ銀行の株式取得を開始。コメルツ銀行からの激しい反対や、ドイツ政府からの批判を受けながらも持ち株比率を高めてきた。

ウニクレディトのアンドレア・オルチェル最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）はコメルツ銀行に対し、策定した経営戦略に則って利益を増やすように要求する一方で、両行の完全合併を２０２９―３０年に先送りしていた。

オルチェル氏はコメルツ銀行の株式取得が完了し次第、同行の監査役会と経営陣を刷新することを示唆している。２７年の定時株主総会を待たずに、株主の承認を求める方針だ。

ドイツ政府側はオルチェル氏との協議で、コメルツ銀行のドイツ・フランクフルトにある本社を維持し、雇用を守り、ドイツ企業への融資を継続するように要求している。

item.title: China says Israel should stop its 'forced establishment' of West Bank settlements
item.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi has told Israeli President Isaac Herzog that Israel should stop and reverse its "forced establishment" of West Bank settlements.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi has told Israeli President Isaac Herzog that Israel should stop and reverse its "forced establishment" of West Bank settlements. China has consistently held that the Palestinian question is the greatest historical injustice of this century, Wang told Herzog during a meeting in Azerbaijan, according to a statement by the Chinese foreign ministry on Friday. Herzog said in a post on X that the meeting, which took place on Thursday, focused on "relations between our countries and the situation in the Middle East". His office declined to comment when asked about their discussions on the West Bank or the Palestinians. Wang said that promoting peace and reconciliation in the region is the "cornerstone" of China's Middle East policy China believes that the "two-state solution" is the right path to a resolution and the immediate priority is to fully open access to the Gaza Strip so a humanitarian "catastrophe" is not allowed to spread, Wang added China is willing to work with the international community to push all parties to return to dialogue and consultation as soon as possible and seek a political settlement of the conflict, Wang said China has long been a supporter of the Palestinian cause and also has close ties with Israel's main regional foe, Iran
