item.title: How Spain's housing crisis sparked nationwide protests and a snap election
item.description: Spain's housing crisis has sparked protests over soaring rents, evictions and holiday rentals. PM Pedro Sanchez has called a snap election for November 29 after parliament rejected housing measures ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / How Spain's housing crisis sparked nationwide protests and a snap election

How Spain's housing crisis sparked nationwide protests and a snap election Spain's housing crisis has sparked protests over soaring rents, evictions and holiday rentals. PM Pedro Sanchez has called a snap election for November 29 after parliament rejected housing measures

Protesters want the government to treat housing as a basic need rather than an asset primarily used to generate profits. (Photo: Screengrab/Reuters)

Rimjhim Singh New Delhi 6 min read Last Updated : Oct 16 2026 | 1:12 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Spain’s worsening housing crisis has triggered protests across the country, putting Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez under pressure and turning affordable housing into a major issue ahead of the next general election.   Protests in Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia and Malaga have brought together tenants, housing activists and residents angry about rising rents, evictions and the difficulty of finding affordable homes. The attempted eviction of an 87-year-old woman in Madrid became a symbol of the crisis.   The protests have added to pressure on Sanchez’s government, which has struggled to secure parliamentary support for emergency housing measures. Sanchez announced a snap general election for November 29, 2026, bringing the vote forward from 2027.

What are the protests about?   Protesters want the government to treat housing as a basic need rather than an asset primarily used to generate profits. Their demands include stronger protection for tenants, measures to prevent evictions and steps to bring rents within reach of ordinary households.   According to Reuters , Spain faces a housing shortage of about 750,000 homes, a figure that the Bank of Spain expects to rise to more than one million by 2028. Also Read

US judge orders Trump administration to reopen Green Card lottery by Nov 1

Can AI 'feel' pain? Anthropic bans 'cruel' behaviour towards its models

Can every citizen claim to be journalist? SC says issue needs 'examination'

Delhi property tax waiver extended to Dec 31: Claim process explained

US scraps 540-day work permit extension: What immigrant workers must know

The attempted eviction of María del Carmen Abascal, an 87-year-old pensioner in Madrid, became a rallying point for the movement. Her case highlighted the difficulties faced by vulnerable residents who risk losing their homes in an increasingly expensive market. Fox News reported that her death on October 7 further intensified public anger.

Protesters have called for stronger tenant protections, limits on rent increases and action against property speculation. They also want the government to increase the supply of affordable housing and prevent evictions that leave vulnerable people without a home.   Tourism and property speculation add to the crisis   Mass tourism has become another source of tension, particularly in Barcelona, where residents blame the growth of holiday rentals for reducing the supply of homes available to permanent residents. Some property owners prefer short-term tourist rentals because they can be more profitable than long-term leases.   According to Fox News , Barcelona and the surrounding region received 26.1 million visitors in 2025, generating an estimated $15.4 billion in direct tourism spending.

Housing activists argue that the growth of short-term holiday rentals reduces the supply of homes available to permanent residents and puts upward pressure on rents. Research cited by the European Parliament has linked the concentration of short-term rentals in some Barcelona neighbourhoods to rising housing costs and the displacement of residents.   Tourism is not the only cause of the crisis. A shortage of homes, rising demand, property investment and the gap between wages and rents have all contributed. However, the growth of holiday rentals has made the conflict between visitors and residents more visible.   The Spanish government has proposed restricting corporate purchases of residential property as part of its efforts to curb speculation and address the housing shortage. However, the proposals have drawn criticism from property developers. Carolina Roca, president of the Association of Property Developers of Madrid, told Reuters that the legal uncertainty created by the decrees could slow investment in affordable housing.

What are protesters demanding?   Protesters want housing to be treated as a basic need rather than an asset primarily used to generate profits. Their demands include rent controls, stronger protection against evictions, restrictions on short-term rentals and more public and affordable housing.   The crisis has also drawn in Spain's trade unions. The country's two largest unions, the General Union of Workers (UGT) and the Workers' Commissions (CCOO), announced plans for a nationwide general strike on November 11, Reuters reported. The proposed strike is scheduled just over two weeks before the election.   Valeria Racu, a spokesperson for the Tenants' Union, told Reuters : "We cannot ignore the fact that housing is where most of our wages go. What is the point of raising the minimum wage if housing costs are rising three, four or five times faster?"

Reuters reported that the average monthly rent of €1,176 was equivalent to about 98.7 per cent of a young person's average monthly salary in Spain, citing the Youth Council of Spain. The figures show why housing has become a major concern for workers who may be employed but still struggle to afford a place to live.   Why did parliament reject Sanchez's housing measures?   Sanchez's government approved emergency housing measures on September 29. The proposals included extending protections against eviction for vulnerable tenants, limiting rent increases and regulating short-term and seasonal rentals.   According to the Spanish government's announcements, the package also included tax incentives for landlords offering affordable rents, interest-free loans of up to €50,000 for first-time homebuyers and funding to support social housing construction. The government proposed restricting purchases of residential property by investment funds accused of profiting from the shortage.

On October 2, parliament rejected the emergency housing package. The conservative People's Party (PP), the far-right Vox and Catalan separatist party Junts opposed the measures. Opposition parties argued that the proposals could create uncertainty for landlords and investors, discourage construction and reduce the supply of rental homes.   The government approved two housing decrees again on October 6, including measures to cap rent increases, temporarily restrict evictions and limit corporate purchases of residential property. Reuters reported that the rules would initially take effect through emergency legislation but would still require parliamentary approval. A separate proposal for the automatic renewal of rental contracts also needed support.

Sanchez defended the measures as necessary to protect tenants and tackle speculation. Reuters quoted him as saying they were "based on plain common sense". He also said the measures would "protect the most vulnerable".   Why did Sanchez call a snap election?   Sanchez announced on October 5 that Spain would hold a general election on November 29, bringing the vote forward from 2027.   The immediate trigger was the failure to secure parliamentary support for the government's housing measures.   A snap election is a vote held earlier than originally expected. In Spain, the prime minister can initiate an early election by requesting the dissolution of parliament under the constitutional process. The result will determine the composition of the national parliament, including the Congress of Deputies, which plays a central role in selecting the prime minister and approving legislation.

item.description:

[１５日 ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）向けクラウドサービスを...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
情報ＢＯＸ：コアウィーブ巨額債務に広がる懸念、問われるＡＩブームの持続性 9:25 配信

コアウィーブのロゴ。2026年7月20日撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo

Anhata Rooprai　Aditya Soni

[１５日 ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）向けクラウドサービスを手掛けるコアウィーブの債務急増を受け、投資家の間でＡＩブームの持続可能性に対する懸念が強まっている。市場に広がるのは、データセンター建設のために借り入れが膨らむ一方、その投資を正当化できるだけの需要が本当に見込めるのかという疑問だ。

エヌビディアが支援するコアウィーブの株式と社債は、マイク・イントレーター最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）が契約残高の強さを強調したにもかかわらず下落した。この動きはテクノロジー株全体の売りを誘発している。

投資家が何を懸念しているのか、そして同社の問題がＡＩ業界全体にどのような影響を与える可能性があるのかをまとめた。

◎コアウィーブとは

コアウィーブは、エヌビディア製プロセッサーによる計算能力を、マイクロソフトやオープンＡＩなどＡＩの開発・運用を行う企業へ貸し出している。「ネオクラウド」と呼ばれる新興クラウド事業者の代表格で、高価かつ供給が限られるＡＩ向け半導体への需要増加を背景に急成長してきた。

ネオクラウド企業は、顧客が自前でデータセンターを建設しなくてもＡＩ向け計算資源を利用できるようにする。ただ、そのサービス提供には半導体やインフラへの巨額な先行投資が必要となり、多くの場合は借り入れによって資金が賄われている。

◎財務状況

コアウィーブはこれまで一度も最終黒字化を達成していない半面、ＬＳＥＧのデータによると負債総額は約５００億ドルに上っている。

８月には年間設備投資計画を４０億ドル引き上げ、３５０億─３９０億ドルに拡大した。アナリストは今年の売上高を約１３０億ドルと予想する一方、２１億３０００万ドルの赤字を見込む。

同社の２０３１年償還のジャンク債利回りは約１６％まで上昇した。債務不履行リスクを保証するためのクレジット・デフォルト・スワップ（ＣＤＳ）コストも約１０００ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）に達し、債権者の警戒感が強まっていることがうかがえる。

これに対しイントレーター氏は、ロイターが確認した社内メモの中で、契約残高は債務返済に十分対応できる水準だと説明した。同社の第２・四半期末時点の売上契約残高は１０４２億ドルで、第３・四半期初めにはさらに２５０億ドル超の新規契約が積み上がったという。

エヌビディアのジェンスン・フアンＣＥＯも懸念を一蹴。コアウィーブの財務体質は改善しているとして、救済支援の必要性はないとの見解を示した。またエヌビディアは、３２年４月まで売れ残ったコアウィーブの計算能力を買い取る契約を結んでいる。

◎「炭鉱のカナリア」か

コアウィーブの事業は（１）ＡＩ計算需要の拡大（２）それを支える設備投資に対して金融市場が資金を供給し続けること、という２つの要素に依存している。

同社は強い需要を主張しているが、株価下落は投資家が資金調達面に不安を抱いていることを物語る。

市場が恐れているのは、ＡＩ需要自体が突然消滅することではない。むしろ、借入コストが上昇した中で需要が予想以上に鈍化した場合、現在の事業モデルが維持できなくなるリスクだ。

ＩＧグループのチーフ・テクニカル・アナリスト、アクセル・ルドルフ氏は「これはＡＩ計算需要への関心が急減したというよりも、その拡大資金をどのように調達しているかに対する投資家の疑問を反映している」と指摘した。

ＸＴＢのリサーチディレクター、キャスリーン・ブルックス氏は「コアウィーブは急速にＡＩ投資テーマ全体の『炭鉱のカナリア（危険信号）』になりつつある」と述べた。

◎市場が神経質な理由

投資家が疑問視しているのは、ＡＩから生まれる収益が、インフラ建設と資金調達にかかる膨大なコストの増加ペースに追い付けるのかどうかだ。コアウィーブは契約収入を得る前に巨額投資を行う必要がある。金利が上昇すれば資金調達コストはさらに膨らみ、収益性は一段と圧迫される。

さらに、半導体そのものにもリスクがある。新世代チップが登場すると既存チップの価値は急速に低下するため、事業者は継続的な更新投資を迫られる。

こうした懸念はコアウィーブだけの問題ではない。米国の大手テクノロジー企業による今年のＡＩインフラ投資額は、合計で７０００億ドルを超えると見込まれているからだ。

◎懸念される悪影響

最も懸念されるシナリオは、ＡＩインフラ向け融資市場全体が引き締まる展開。貸し手がより高い利回りを要求したり、ＡＩ関連プロジェクトへの融資に慎重になったりすれば、多くの事業者は設備拡張計画の縮小を迫られる恐れが出てくる。その結果、サーバーや半導体などの設備需要が鈍化し、顧客が期待する計算能力の供給にも影響が及びかねない。

今回の問題が「ＡＩ投資ブームは収益創出能力を上回るペースで進んでいるのではないか」という疑念を一段と強めれば、テクノロジー株全体への売り圧力が高まる可能性もある。

もっとも、コアウィーブが経営危機に陥ったとしても、その影響の大きさは事業再編の内容次第であり、大手テクノロジー企業との関係だけを理由に金融システム全体へ波及するような危機に発展するとは限らない。

◎他にリスク企業は

ガートナーは、ネオクラウド事業者の約８０％が３０年までに事業継続できなくなる可能性があると予測している。期待されるＡＩ収益だけでは、計画されている全てのインフラ投資を採算ベースに乗せることは難しいという見方だ。

今回のテクノロジー銘柄売りでは、ネオクラウド企業のネビウス、アプライドデジタル、アイレンの株価も下落した。オープンＡＩへの大型投資を進めるソフトバンクグループについても、信用リスクをヘッジするコストが上昇している。

アマゾン・ドット・コム、グーグル親会社アルファベット、メタ、エヌビディアも社債スプレッドは過去最高水準まで拡大しているが、その上昇ペースはコアウィーブほど急ではなく、これらの企業にはより大きなキャッシュフローと強固な財務基盤がある。

item.description: [１５日 ロイター] - 米シカゴ地区連銀のグールズビー総裁は１５日、今週発表された９月の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
予想上回るインフレは気が重いが、まだ楽観＝米シカゴ連銀総裁 9:23 配信

米シカゴ地区連銀のグールズビー総裁。2026年8月27日、米ワイオミング州ジャクソンホールで撮影。REUTERS/Ann Saphir/File Photo

[１５日 ロイター] - 米シカゴ地区連銀のグールズビー総裁は１５日、今週発表された９月の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）および卸売物価指数（ＰＰＩ）の上昇率が予想を上回ったことについて、「気が重くなる」と述べた。

同氏はＣＮＮのインタビューで「インフレの要因が、関税であれ、中東の紛争や供給の混乱であれ、短期間で解消可能なものであるならば、それは最良のシナリオだと、私はまだ楽観視している」と発言。

その上で「もし、それが需要の過熱や人工知能（ＡＩ）データセンターの拡張に起因するものであるなら、それはもう少し懸念すべき事態であり、われわれはそれに対処しなければならないだろう」と語った。

item.content:encoded:
6月日銀利上げに議決延期請求検討した事実ない＝城内経財相 9:00 配信

城内実経済財政相。10月15日、都内で撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

Yoshifumi Takemoto

［東京　１６日　ロイター］ - 城内実経済財政相 は１６日の閣議後会見で、日銀が６月に利上げを決定した際に議決延期請求を検討した事実はないと述べ、６月の日銀金融政策決定会合前に内閣府幹部らとの話の中で議決延期請求に言及したとする一部報道を否定した。

１４日の毎日新聞に、自身の日銀会合への出席回数の多さが「異例」で金融政策に目を光らせていると記述されたことに関しても、城内氏は、出席は日銀法に定められた正式な職務とし、「今後も日程の都合がつけば出席したい」と語った。

item.description: ［東京 １６日 ロイター］ - 三井物産は１５日、米ペンスキー・コーポレーション（ＰＣ）と共同で同社傘下の自動車販売...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
三井物、米自動車販売大手を非公開化へ　米社と追加出資 8:56 配信

［東京　１６日　ロイター］ - 三井物産は１５日、米ペンスキー・コーポレーション（ＰＣ）と共同で同社傘下の自動車販売大手ペンスキー・オートモーティブ・グループ（ＰＡＧ）の全浮動株の取得を決めたと発表した。想定取得価格は約３９億ドル（約５８５０億円）。三井物の出資比率は約２０．３％から約３６％に、ＰＣは約５２．１％から約６４％になる。

１株当たりの買付価格は２１２ドル。浮動株取得は関係当局の承認などを条件に２０２７年３月期第４・四半期の完了を見込む。三井物の通期連結業績に与える影響は軽微だが、来期以降は持ち分比率の上昇に伴い、中期経営計画の前提に織り込んでいない収益貢献を見込む。

三井物とＰＣは７月に法的拘束力のない非公開化を提案していた。今回、ＰＡＧの特別委員会の推奨を受け、同社取締役会が承認した。

item.title: 中国で「アップルインテリジェンス」承認とクック氏、現地報道
item.description: [北京 １５日 ロイター] - 米アップルのティム・クック会長は、人工知能（ＡＩ）サービス「アップルインテリジェンス...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国で「アップルインテリジェンス」承認とクック氏、現地報道 8:04 配信

アップルのティム・クック会長。2025年9月9日、米カリフォルニア州クパチーノにあるアップル本社で撮影。REUTERS/Manuel Orbegozo

[北京 １５日 ロイター] - 米アップルのティム・クック会長は、人工知能（ＡＩ）サービス「アップルインテリジェンス」が中国で承認され、１０月中にテスト版を提供する予定だと明らかにした。中国の政府系メディア、澎湃新聞が１５日に上海で行った独占インタビューとして報じた。

• クック氏は澎湃新聞に対し、テスト版にはライブ翻訳、文章作成ツールなどの機能が搭載されるが、「Ｓｉｒｉ（シリ）ＡＩ」は含まれないと述べた。

• ロイターはこれまでに、アップルが中国市場向けに特化した大規模言語モデル（ＬＬＭ）を訓練し、中国でのＡＩ機能の実装で第三者企業のモデルに依存してきた戦略から転換したと報じた。

• ＡＩモデルは中国のテクノロジー大手アリババ・グループとの提携で開発・訓練されたという。

• 中国のインターネット規制当局は７月、アップルのオンデバイス型生成ＡＩサービス「アップルインテリジェンス」が、中国国内のｉＰｈｏｎｅ向けに登録されたと発表していた。

• 中国商務省によると、クック氏は１５日に王文濤商務相と会談し、ＡＩの発展やアップルの中国事業について協議した。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：米アップル、ＥＶ断念でもＡＩによる収益化期待揺るがず アングル：アップル初の折り畳みｉＰｈｏｎｅ、強気価格が突きつける「誰のためのスマホか」 アングル：クック氏からターナス氏へ、アップル新体制にＡＩと「脱中国」の試練 焦点：ＡＩ時代のアップル、過去の「強み」は足かせとなるか コラム：クック氏退任のアップル、ＡＩ時代でｉＰｈｏｎｅ依存脱却なるか 最終更新: 10/16(金) 8:04 ロイター

item.content:encoded:
グーグルＡＩ向けニュース提供、ＣＮＮやアクシオスなど新たに参加 7:59 配信

CNNのロゴ。2019年7月30日、米デトロイトで撮影。REUTERS/Brian Snyder

[１５日 ロイター] - 米グーグルが展開する人工知能（ＡＩ）向けニュースライセンス・プログラムに、ＣＮＮや英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（ＦＴ）、米アクシオスなどの報道機関が参加した。グーグルは１５日、生成ＡＩ機能向けに報道コンテンツの利用許諾を得るとともに、各社と読者エンゲージメント拡大の手法を模索すると発表した。

グーグルによると、このプログラムは昨年、米紙ワシントン・ポストなどを対象に試験的に開始され、現在は世界で４００超の出版・報道機関が参加している。

今回の契約は、パラマウント・スカイダンスによるワーナー・ブラザース・ディスカバリー買収完了後、新会社スカイダンス 傘下となったＣＮＮにとって初の提携案件となる。スカイダンスのデービッド・エリソン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は、新会社をテクノロジー主導のメディア企業として位置付ける方針を示している。

契約の一環として、参加する報道機関はグーグルに拡張的なコンテンツ利用権を付与し、グーグルは新たなＡＩ機能の開発を進める一方で、コンテンツ提供の対価を各社に支払う。契約金額は公表されていない。

ＣＮＮの戦略的提携・事業開発担当シニアバイスプレジデント、サム・フェリックス氏は「生成ＡＩを巡るグーグルの技術革新は、人々が情報やコンテンツを見つける方法を変えた。こうしたツールにより、視聴者や読者との新たな接点を探ることができる」とコメントした。

グーグルは、ＡＩ機能において記事の出典を明確に表示し、元記事へのリンクを付与することで、利用者が信頼する情報源にアクセスできるようにするとしている。

報道機関はＡＩ企業による大規模言語モデルの学習への無断利用を防ぐため、法的対応を強化しつつある。また検索エンジン各社がＡＩによる回答を表示する機能を導入し、利用者がニュースサイトを訪問せずに情報を得られるようになった影響で、報道機関は検索経由の流入減少という課題にも直面している。

ＣＮＮは今回の契約について、知的財産権を保護する戦略に沿ったものだと説明した。同社は複数の企業と商業提携を結んでいるほか、他の業界関係者とも協議を続けているという。

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米年末商戦、支出は慎重も堅調な見通し　小売業協会4.2％増と予測 7:41 配信

クリスマス商戦のディスプレー。2025年11月21日、米ニュージャージー州のウォルマートで撮影。REUTERS/Mike Segar

[１５日 ロイター] - 全米小売業協会（ＮＲＦ）は１５日、２０２６年１１―１２月の米国の年末商戦売上高が前年同期比４．２％増の１兆０１３０億ドルになるとの予測を発表した。伸び率は前年同期の３．１％から拡大すると見込んだ。

消費者の購買力が引き続き堅調に推移するとの見方を示し、ＮＲＦのマシュー・シェイ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は「今年の予測は、消費者が予算に気を配りつつも、年末の購買を優先するだろうとの私たちの確信に基づいている」とコメントした。

詳細は以下の通り。

・２０２５年の年末商戦は前年同期比で３．１％増の９７２０億ドルだった。

・ＮＲＦによると、予測は個人消費、雇用、賃金、および過去の小売売上高のデータを組み込んだ経済モデルに基づいている。自動車、ガソリン、飲食店の売上高は除外されている。

・インフレが進んだことに伴う生活費の増加により、消費者は購買行動をより慎重にしている。ウォルマート 、コールズ 、アメリカン・イーグル などの小売企業は極めて重要な年末商戦を控え、個人消費への圧力が強まっていると指摘している。

・デロイトが１５日公表した約４０００人の米消費者への調査によると、２６年の年末商戦で１世帯当たりの平均支出額は前年同期比４％増の１６５４ドルに達する見込み。Ｚ世代（２０―２９歳）や、３０―４５歳のミレニアル世代の支出増がけん引すると見込んだ。

・デロイトは年末商戦で１世帯当たりのモノ消費が前年同期比１０％増の９８８ドルになると予想。一方コト消費は４％減の６６６ドルと見込んだ。体験型の贈り物を予定する消費者の７９％は、実物の商品を組み合わせることを計画している。

item.title: Rotting meat smell sparks protest at Mexico's screwworm sterile-fly plant
item.description: A rotten smell hanging over a town in Mexico's southern Chiapas state drove residents into the streets on Thursday to demand the removal of a sterile-fly plant at the center of the US-Mexican fight against the flesh-eating New World screwworm parasite.
item.dc:creator: Jose Torres, Cassandra Garrison
item.content:encoded: A rotten smell hanging over a town in Mexico's southern Chiapas state drove residents into the streets on Thursday to demand the removal of a sterile-fly plant at the center of the US-Mexican fight against the flesh-eating New World screwworm parasite. Residents in Metapa de Dominguez compared the odor to rotting meat and spoiled food, describing it as “pungent in your nose and mouth” and causing nausea. The smell, once concentrated around the plant, could now be detected farther away, particularly when winds carried it across the town, protesters said. The odor had reached schools near the plant and disrupted classes. "We don't care about the investment they made. What we want is for this plant to leave here, because the smell coming over the town is too much," said truck driver Mercedes Becerra de la Cruz. The complaints come less than four months after Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and US Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins [USN:L6N42X14F TEXT:"inaugurated"] the facility on June 27. The US Department of Agriculture invested $21 million toward the $51 million facility, part of a broader effort to halt a screwworm outbreak that disrupted the cross-border cattle trade. Sterile flies are the main defense against screwworm, a parasite whose larvae burrow into the living flesh of cattle and other warm-blooded animals and can kill them if untreated. Eradicated from the US decades ago, the pest has surged north from Central America through Mexico, prompting Washington to impose a more than year-long ban on Mexican cattle imports. The Metapa plant is expected eventually to produce 100 million sterile flies a week. Mexico has recorded nearly 48,000 cases of screwworm in the current outbreak and the United States 53. Inside the Metapa plant, millions of flies are bred each week, their larvae fed a carefully formulated mixture of egg, milk and powdered hemoglobin that mimics the nutrient-rich conditions of a wound. The flies are sterilized before being released by the millions to mate with wild females without producing offspring, gradually suppressing the population. Outside its walls, residents said daily life has increasingly been shaped by an overpowering odor that drifts into surrounding neighborhoods and schools. "We need the federal government to respond and have the plant relocated. It is far too close, right in the middle of the town," said 49-year-old homemaker Rosalba Merida Herrera. "For the sake of our children and our elderly, we are asking them to look at the situation, as this issue is now affecting the entire town." A spokesperson for Mexico's Agriculture Ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: 米ＡＩ企業専門家、ディープフェイク精度向上で裁判の証拠判断困難と警告
item.description:
Nate Raymond
[１５日 ロイター] - 米オープンＡＩや米メタ・プラットフォームズの技術専門家らは１５日、...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米ＡＩ企業専門家、ディープフェイク精度向上で裁判の証拠判断困難と警告 7:22 配信

AIの文字。2025年12月11日、米パロアルトで撮影。REUTERS/Carlos Barria

Nate Raymond

[１５日 ロイター] - 米オープンＡＩや米メタ・プラットフォームズの技術専門家らは１５日、連邦裁判所の証拠規則を検討する司法会議の諮問委員会の会合で、生成人工知能（ＡＩ）による偽造映像や音声「ディープフェイク」の精度が急速に向上しており、裁判で提出される証拠の真偽を見極めることが一段と難しくなるとの見方を示した。

会合はボストンで開かれ、業界や学界、政府関係者らが参加した。委員会は２０２３年以降、ディープフェイクによる証拠偽造への対応や、ＡＩ生成コンテンツの信頼性をどのように認定するかについて検討を続けている。

オープンＡＩの政策顧問シラ・アンダーソン氏は「ＡＩ画像は今後さらに高度化する。将来的に科学的な手法で検出できるとは思わない」と述べた。

メタでプロダクトマネジメント部門の責任者を務めるデビン・ノーダー氏は「最新世代のモデルが生成する映像は、人間には本物かＡＩ生成か区別がつかない。作成に必要なコストと時間も極めて小さい」と警告した。

今のところ司法が把握している実例は依然として限られている。連邦司法センターが３月に公表した調査によると、回答した９３１人の裁判官のうち、提出された証拠がディープフェイクだとして異議が申し立てられた案件を経験したのは１５人だった。委員会の委員長を務めるニューヨーク州南部地区連邦地裁のジェシー・ファーマン判事は「裁判所がディープフェイクに直面するとの予測は多いが、実際の事例はまだそれほど多くない」と述べ、新たな小委員会を設置して検討を続ける方針を示した。

オープンＡＩやメタなどは、映像の真正性を確認する仕組みの導入を進めているところだ。カリフォルニア州や欧州連合（ＥＵ）では、ディープフェイク検出を目的とした電子透かし（ウオーターマーク）の付与を義務付ける法制度も整備されている。

ただアンダーソン氏は「各社で仕組みが異なり、全ての透かしを確実に検出したり、映像の真正性を一律に検証したりする方法はない。技術は改善し続けるだろうが、完全なものにはならない」とくぎを刺した。

これに対し、委員を務めるニューヨーク州南部地区連邦地裁のバレリー・カプローニ判事は、ＡＩに特化した新たな証拠規則の策定には慎重な姿勢を表明。「虚偽の証拠提出は従来から違法であり、裁判官には証拠が偽造かどうかを判断する権限がある」と指摘した上で、虚偽の証拠を持ち込むというのは昔からある問題だと付け加えた。

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ市場サマリー（15日）ドル下落、Ｓ＆Ｐ５００上昇　利回り低下 7:20 配信

＜為替＞ ドルが円やユーロなどの主要通貨に対し下落した。連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）当局者の慎重な発言を受け１０月の利上げ観測が後退しているほか、この日発表された堅調な物価・消費関連指標よりもＡＩ（人工知能）向けデータセンター関連企業を巡る懸念に市場の関心が集まったことがドルの重しになった。

この日発表の米経済指標では、９月の小売売上高が前月比０．８％増加。ガソリン価格の上昇を背景に予想を上回る伸びとなったが、ガソリン以外の支出は総じて緩やかで、自動車、ガソリン、建設資材、外食サービスを除くコア小売売上高は前月比０．１％増と、伸びは前月から鈍化した。

９月の卸売物価指数（ＰＰＩ、最終需要向け財・サービス）は前年比６．３％上昇。２０２２年１２月以来の大幅な伸びとなり、エネルギー関連以外にもインフレが広がっている可能性が改めて示された。

市場ではＦＲＢの金融政策の行方を見極めようと、ウォーシュＦＲＢ議長が１６日にバンコクで開かれる国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）・世界銀行年次総会で行う講演が注目されている。

終盤の取引で主要通貨に対するドル指数は０．４５％安の１０１．９９。前日は１年６カ月ぶりの高値を付けていた。

ユーロは対ドルで０．５６％高の１．１２１８ドル。円は対ドルで０．１５％高の１５８．０８円。

ＮＹ外為市場：[USD/J]

＜債券＞ 国債利回りが低下した。ＡＩ（人工知能）関連成長の鈍化懸念のほか、連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が今月末の会合で政策金利を据え置くとの観測を背景に長期利回りが特に低下し、１０年債と３０年債の利回りは９月２３日以来の低水準を付けた。

ウォーシュＦＲＢ議長は１６日午前にバンコクで開かれる国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）・世界銀行年次総会で講演を行う予定。ＦＲＢの金融政策の手掛かりを得ようと注目されているが、シュワブ金融調査センターの債券調査・戦略責任者、コリン・マーティン氏は、ウォーシュ氏が今回の講演で新たな政策の方向性を示す可能性は低いと予想。「ウォーシュ氏は多くを語らないタイプで、講演で極めて慎重にしか発言しない。今回も変わらないだろう」としている。

終盤の取引で、１０年債利回りは１０．１ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）低下の５．０８９％。１日としての低下幅は２０２５年８月上旬以降最大となる。

３０年債利回りは９．８ｂｐ低下の５．４２６％。１日としての低下幅は２５年１０月１０日以降で最大。

２年債利回りは５．３ｂｐ低下の４．７４９％。一時は９月１８日以来の低水準を付けた。２年債利回りと１０年債利回りの格差は３３．８ｂｐ。

米金融・債券市場：[US/BJ]

＜株式＞ Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種が序盤の下げから持ち直し、上昇して取引を終えた。人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株を懸念する投資家が、イーライリリー、ユナイテッドヘルスなどのヘルスケア株やウォルマートなど消費関連株に資金を移した。

ハイテク株の一角は下落した。投資家は、債務負担が大きく金利上昇の影響を受けやすいＡＩ関連企業を精査した。

ドイツ銀行による投資判断の引き上げを受け、イーライリリーは３％超、ユナイテッドヘルスは２．８％、ウォルマートは１．４％それぞれ上昇。この３銘柄がＳ＆Ｐ総合５００種の上昇に大きく寄与した。

エヌビディアは１．８％下落。半導体メーカーの台湾積体電路製造（ＴＳＭＣ）が、ＡＩ関連の旺盛な需要を背景に６四半期連続で過去最高益を記録したものの、２０２７年の見通しについて慎重な見方を示したことを受けた。

サーバーメーカーのデル・テクノロジーズは６．９％、ヒューレット・パッカード・エンタープライズは７．１％それぞれ下落。借り入れコスト上昇の影響を受けやすいＡＩ関連企業への懸念から、両社株は前日の急落に続いて値を下げた。

米国株式市場：[.NJP]

＜金先物＞ 米卸売物価指数（ＰＰＩ）が予想を上回る伸びとなったものの、ドル安と米長期金利の低下を背景に反発し、３営業日ぶりに上昇した。中心限月１２月物の清算値（終値に相当）は前日比１．５％高の１オンス＝４１７０．１０ドル。スポット価格も１．２％高の４１５３．４２ドルとなった。

ＮＹ貴金属：[GOL/XJ]

＜米原油先物＞ 米国が世界のタンカー「影の船団」に対する規制を緩和する可能性を投資家が見極める中、北海ブレント先物はほぼ横ばいとなった。一方、中東情勢を巡る地政学リスクのプレミアムが相場を下支えした。北海ブレント先物の清算値（終値に相当）は前日比０．１４ドル（０．１３％）安の１バレル＝１０５．９２ドル。米ＷＴＩ先物は、米原油在庫の大幅な取り崩しが相場を支え、２．８８ドル（３．０３％）高の９７．９７ドルで清算した。

item.description:
Milana Vinn Anirban Sen
[ニューヨーク １５日 ロイター] - 米生成人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
アンソロピック評価、ＩＰＯ参加検討の投資家が引き下げも＝関係者 7:08 配信

アンソロピックのロゴ。9月17日、米サンフランシスコで撮影。REUTERS/Carlos Barria

Milana Vinn　Anirban Sen

[ニューヨーク １５日 ロイター] - 米生成人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックの既存投資家や今後の新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）への参加を検討している投資家の一部が、同社の最新の財務開示を受けて企業価値評価の引き下げを検討している。関係者４人が明らかにした。ＡＩ開発コストの膨張に対する市場の懸念が背景にある。

関係者によると、１４日に米サンフランシスコで開かれた投資家説明会の一部参加者の間では、アンソロピックの企業価値を約１兆５０００億ドルとする見方が浮上した。１１月のＩＰＯを前に市場で想定されていた約２兆ドルを大幅に下回る水準だ。

説明会でアンソロピックは、２０２６年７─９月期の売上高は前期比４５％増の１６８億ドルとなり、調整後ベースで黒字を確保したと明らかにした。

これらの数字はＡＩシステム開発に伴う巨額投資への懸念を一定程度和らげたものの、売上高の増加率鈍化を失望視する投資家もいた。アンソロピックの売上高は２６年１─３月期から４－６月期にかけて２倍超に伸びていた。

アンソロピックはコメント要請に直ちには応じなかった。

アンソロピックのＩＰＯにおける評価が低調となれば、ＡＩ市場全体にも影響が及びかねない。投資家の多くは、ＡＩ業界の短期的な成長見通しがアンソロピックの上場成功と、その後に見込まれる同業オープンＡＩの上場計画に大きく左右されるとみているからだ。

足元では世界的なハイテク株安が進み、ＡＩ関連インフラ企業や半導体メーカー、ＡＩ向け計算資源を貸し出す「ネオクラウド」事業者の株価に打撃を与えている。エヌビディアが出資するコアウィーブの株式や社債も１５日に下落し、借入金への依存を強めるＡＩインフラ投資に対する警戒感が映し出された。

アンソロピックのＩＰＯが期待を下回れば、こうした懸念に拍車をかけてもおかしくない。

投資家説明会にはアンソロピックの主要投資家らが出席し、ダリオ・アモデイ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）とクリシュナ・ラオ最高財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）が事業戦略などを伝えた。

item.title: インフレ期待悪化なら積極的な利上げ必要も＝クリーブランド連銀総裁
item.description:
Michael S. Derby
[１５日 ロイター] - 米クリーブランド地区連銀のハマック総裁は１５日、国民のイ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
インフレ期待悪化なら積極的な利上げ必要も＝クリーブランド連銀総裁 7:05 配信

米クリーブランド地区連銀のハマック総裁。8月27日、ワイオミング州ジャクソンホールで撮影。REUTERS/Ann Saphir

Michael S. Derby

[１５日 ロイター] - 米クリーブランド地区連銀のハマック総裁は１５日、国民のインフレ期待が著しく悪化すれば、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）は一段と積極的な利上げが必要になる可能性があるとの見方を示した。

ニューヨークで開かれたゴールドマン・サックス主催のイベントで「私が懸念しているのは、インフレ心理が生まれ、物価上昇圧力がますます根強いものになるとの期待が定着すれば、金融政策が果たすべき役割を果たすのが一段と難しくなり、インフレ心理が定着していない場合よりも大幅な政策対応が必要になるかもしれないということだ」と述べた。

現在の状況が金融政策にとって何を意味するのかについて明確な指針は示さなかったが、ハマック氏は利上げによる高インフレ圧力への対応を早くから強く支持してきた。

同氏は、借り入れコストの上昇にもかかわらずテクノロジーなどへの投資が速いペースで進んでいることを踏まえ、足元の金融環境はおおむね中立的との見方を示した。その上で「現時点で金融環境が経済活動を抑制しているとは感じていない」と述べた。

item.title: Lisandro Martinez issues apology for post-match remarks on Manchester United's hierarchy
item.description: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has issued an apology on social media after criticising the club's board following the team's 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday (local time).
item.content:encoded:
Lisandro Martinez issues apology for post-match remarks on Manchester United's hierarchy Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has issued an apology on social media after criticising the club's board following the team's 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday (local time). ANI | Updated: 16-10-2026 10:02 IST | Created: 16-10-2026 10:02 IST

Lisandro Martinez (Photo: Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has issued an apology on social media after criticising the club's board following the team's 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday (local time). Martinez had criticised the club's hierarchy and said he expects more from the team’s technical director following their defeat, calling for greater investment in the squad to compete with rival teams. In a post-match interview, Martinez said he had expected the club's management to bring in more players during the summer transfer window, specifically expressing disappointment with technical director Jason Wilcox. Now in an Instagram story, Martinez has apologised for his post-match comments and said he met Manchester United's leadership and manager Michael Carrick, describing the discussion as positive. He said his frustration after the defeat led him to express his views at the wrong time and place, acknowledged that his remarks did not help unite the club, and stressed that everyone was working towards Manchester United's shared goal of success. “Today I met with the club's leadership and the manager. It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday's game. Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity. The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise,” he said. “Our club is at its best when we are all united, and I recognise that my words in that moment did not help with that. I know that every single person at Manchester United is doing everything possible to achieve our shared ambition: bringing the success that this club and its supporters deserve. With this situation now behind us, we are fully focused on winning together,” he added. (ANI)

item.title: Magnitude 7.0 earthquake jolts Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula; no tsunami threat issued
item.description: An earthquake of magnitude 7.0 on the Richter scale struck Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula region on Friday, according to the European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC) and the National Center ...
item.content:encoded:
Magnitude 7.0 earthquake jolts Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula; no tsunami threat issued An earthquake of magnitude 7.0 on the Richter scale struck Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula region on Friday, according to the European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC) and the National Center for Seismology (NCS). ANI | Updated: 16-10-2026 09:56 IST | Created: 16-10-2026 09:56 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Russia

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

An earthquake of magnitude 7.0 on the Richter scale struck Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula region on Friday, according to the European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC) and the National Centre for Seismology (NCS). The US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) said there was no tsunami warning, advisory, watch or threat following the earthquake. According to the NCS, the earthquake occurred at 9:05 am IST today at a depth of 152 km, with its epicentre located at latitude 52.068° North and longitude 157.164° East. The EMSC reported a preliminary magnitude of 7.0, placing the earthquake approximately 123 km southwest of Vilyuchinsk in the Russian Federation. In a post on X, the EMSC said the earthquake had been confirmed by seismic data. Its data separately recorded the event at magnitude 6.9, with a depth of 130 km and coordinates of 52.059° North and 157.234° East. The EMSC placed the earthquake approximately 146 km south-southwest of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, a city with a population of around 187,000, and 80 km north-northeast of Ozernovskiy, which has a population of around 2,600. The US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration recorded the earthquake at magnitude 7.0, with a depth of approximately 148 km, and located it around 415 miles southwest of Bering Island in the Komandorski Islands region. In its assessment, NOAA stated that there was no tsunami warning, advisory, watch or threat. The earthquake's reported magnitude and depth varied slightly across monitoring agencies, with the EMSC recording a magnitude of 6.9 in its detailed data, while the NCS and NOAA reported a magnitude of 7.0. Further details on the impact of the earthquake are awaited. (ANI)

Oct 15 : Meta Platforms on Thursday released an open-weight version of its Muse Spark artificial intelligence model for coding and AI agents, expanding developers' ability to download and adapt the technology. Open-weight models make trained parameters available for developers to modify, unlike proprietary models that remain under their creators' control. They can offer businesses a lower-cost alternative to closed systems. • Meta said Muse Spark has 816 billion total parameters, with 42 billion active at a time, and can handle a context window of up to 1 million tokens • The model can run locally on two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studio computers and is also available through some API providers

item.title: Indonesia gets a 'wake-up call' as MSCI prepares to expel it from global indexes
item.description: Indonesia's stock market is no longer worthy of "emerging market" status, MSCI said on Friday, laying out a plan to remove it from a suite of indexes tracked by funds, a shock move that sparked the steepest one-day drop in Jakarta shares since 1998.
item.dc:creator: Stefanno Sulaiman, Ankur Banerjee
item.content:encoded: Indonesia's stock market is no longer worthy of "emerging market" status, MSCI said on Friday, laying out a plan to remove it from a suite of indexes tracked by funds, a shock move that sparked the steepest one-day drop in Jakarta shares since 1998. The benchmark stock index (.JKSE) , already the world's [USN:L4N43G12X TEXT:"worst performer"] this year, plunged 11% to a six-year low, while the rupiah slid 0.6% to 18,070 per US dollar, its weakest level since late July. Indonesian equities have struggled since January when MSCI froze Indonesia in its indexes and [USN:L6N46202Y TEXT:"threatened a downgrade"] to "frontier" status because of opacity in ownership and trading behaviour. On Friday, MSCI said reforms to address those problems have not made sufficient progress and that even a downgrade to frontier wouldn't reflect the severity of issues. "Significant concerns remain around market dysfunction," MSCI said. "Accordingly, MSCI considers Indonesia's continued classification as an emerging market no longer appropriate," it said in a statement. Instead, it proposed a downgrade to "standalone" status, which would exclude Indonesian stocks from global indexes tracked by billions of dollars in passive investment, forcing funds that follow or are ranked against the indexes to sell. UBS estimated such a move could trigger about $4 billion of passive outflows from Indonesia, with active investors potentially adding a further $15 billion in outflow. Already, foreign investors have net sold $4.7 billion worth of Indonesian stocks in 2026. Coming a month ahead of a scheduled review, MSCI's change of tack [USN:L1N46203P TEXT:"stunned investors"] and irked Jakarta officials. Indonesia's senior economic minister Airlangga Hartarto said there was "a big question mark" over why MSCI did not discuss downgrading the country to "standalone" status during a meeting this week in Bangkok. He made the comment ahead of a meeting of the country's top officials, including the finance minister, the governor of the central bank and other related officials to discuss MSCI's announcement. The Indonesia Stock Exchange said it has taken concrete steps to enhance transparency and integrity in the country's capital market, and CEO Jeffrey Hendrik said he would request further clarification on the basis for the announcement. Angus Mackintosh, an ASEAN specialist at Aletheia Capital in Singapore, said the move did not reflect the health of the vast majority of listed companies or indeed the Indonesian economy, and "grouping Indonesia with Lebanon, Palestine, and Argentina does not make sense." "This is a wake-up call for Indonesia," he said. MSCI SCRUTINY RAISES MORE QUESTIONS MSCI's announcement piles pressure on the government under President Prabowo Subianto. Indonesia has faced a series of setbacks this year, with [USN:L4N3Z114D TEXT:"Moody's"] and [USN:L1N3ZS06T TEXT:"Fitch"] cutting their sovereign rating outlooks to negative, citing reduced policymaking credibility. "The proposal highlights MSCI's dissatisfaction with the pace of reforms and raises further questions about the investability of the market," said Tan Altundag, investment manager for emerging equities at Pictet Asset Management. "The investment implications could be significant," said Altundag, who has no holdings in Indonesia. The office of finance minister Suahasil Nazara, who chairs the country's financial stability board, did not reply to a request for comment. In a sign of investor anxiety over the index provider's move, there was a rush for the exits when the market opened, triggering a 30-minute trading halt on the Jakarta exchange. "It's the first time this has ever happened in my 20 years in the stock market," said Liza Camelia Suryanata, head of research at stockbroker Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia. MSCI's move seemed heavy-handed given the steps Indonesia has taken to [USN:L6N42W0D2 TEXT:"address issues"] around market transparency and increase the free-float requirement for listed firms, Mackintosh said. "The only way for Indonesia to remedy this situation would be to impose severe sanctions and fines on those involved in concerted share manipulation," he said. DOWNGRADE PLANNED FOR MID-2027 MSCI said it will run a consultation with market participants for a downgrade to "standalone" status until April 2027 and then proceed with reclassification unless it finds clear evidence of improvement in market governance and function. Standalone markets are not included in MSCI's emerging or frontier index products, which are tracked by passive funds and treated as performance benchmarks for other fund managers. MSCI says reclassification to standalone status may occur in the case of severe deterioration in market accessibility or size and liquidity, with the most recent example being Argentina. Indonesia, Southeast Asia's biggest economy, would be the largest market to be downgraded to that classification.

ORLANDO, Florida, Oct 15 : The AI equity rout accelerated significantly in Asia on Thursday on growing fears about the murky, circular financing powering the intelligence revolution's buildout, although its force evaporated in European and US trading hours. Still, safe-haven inflows meant US Treasuries had one of their best days in months, despite a surprisingly strong rise in US producer inflation. Today's Key Reads • CoreWeave's slump spotlights growing burden of debt behind AI boom • AI credit worries send default insurance to record high

• AI investment boom may be papering over US economic cracks: Mike Dolan • US producer prices post largest gain in 4-1/2 years; expensive gasoline boosts retail sales • Warsh's quest for quiet Fed gets vocal pushback • Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: Asia in the red, South Korea -7.5 per cent to 6-month low, Japan -5 per cent. UK +1 per cent to 7-week high. Nasdaq +0.1 per cent, S&P 500 +0.3 per cent, Dow +1 per cent.SECTORS/SHARES: Eight sectors on the S&P 500 rise, three fall. Tech -0.5 per cent, energy -1.5 per cent, healthcare +2 per cent. CoreWeave +6.5 per cent, Nike +5 per cent. Hewlett Packard, Dell -7 per cent.FX: Dollar slides, biggest fall in six weeks. Biggest gainer is Swiss franc, +1 per cent; biggest decliner is Brazilian real, -1.5 per cent.BONDS: Bund yield -11 bps to 3.35 per cent, lowest in over a month. US 10-year yield -10 bps to 5.08 per cent, curve flattens. CoreWeave and other AI corporate bonds rise.COMMODITIES/METALS: Oil mixed — Brent flat, WTI +3 per cent. Gold +1 per cent, silver +3 per cent. Today's Talking Points: Funny money The global AI trade has hit some major turbulence. South Korea's KOSPI, a top 10 global index, has lost 20 per cent of its value in barely a week, and on Thursday Japan's Nikkei slid 5 per cent. CoreWeave 2032 bonds issued just four months ago fell below 80 cents in the dollar, typically considered distressed debt levels, and the cost of insuring against major US AI firms defaulting has soared to record levels. As ever, credit markets are likely to lead equities, and the risk of a self-fulfilling doom loop cannot be ignored — selling in certain names casts a shadow over healthier credits, and downgrades and loss of investment-grade ratings could force further selling. All while cash has been spent, and capex is increasingly being financed by debt, private credit and off-balance-sheet borrowing. We're not at crisis point yet — look at the rebound in US stocks and bonds today — but vigilance is required. Bonds be bonds Incoming data shows US producer price inflation is running hotter than expected, like CPI the day before, WTI crude spikes another 3 per cent, and Treasuries rally. Sounds counterintuitive, especially given how heavily fixed income markets have traded in recent weeks, but it shows that the demise of Treasuries' safe-haven appeal has been greatly exaggerated. Thursday was one of the best days of the year for Treasuries, especially for maturities of 10 years and beyond. The question is whether this is a knee-jerk move, or will continued volatility in equities and weakness in AI-related corporate debt remind investors that the best place to hedge, diversify and protect their capital is the traditional "risk-free" asset? Guaranteed nominal yields of over 5 per cent appear to be tempting. Rotation, rotation, rotation Wall Street's resilience on Thursday was pretty remarkable, given the ferocity of the tech selloff in Asia and weight of negative sentiment at the session open. Chip stocks fell for a seventh day, their longest losing streak in four years, but the Nasdaq edged higher and, more impressively, the Dow rose 1 per cent to its highest in a month. As the US earnings season kicks into gear, the focus will be on tech. The bar of expectations is high, and if it is not hurdled, investors may decide to ramp up the rotation into other sectors. How long do rotations out of tech last? According to Deutsche Bank, since mid-2024 the average length of rotation is 67 days and the median is 59 days. In terms of tech drawdowns over these periods, the average is 16.6 per cent and the median is 14.6 per cent. What could move markets tomorrow? • IMF/World Bank meetings in Bangkok, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, ECB President Christine Lagarde, and BoE Governor Andrew Bailey among several officials speaking • Euro zone trade (August) • Euro zone inflation (September, final) • US import prices (September) • US industrial production (September) Want to receive Trading Day in your inbox every weekday morning? item.title: Investors temper Anthropic IPO valuation expectations over revenue growth slowdown, sources say
item.description: Some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors in its upcoming initial public offering are weighing a lower valuation for the AI company after its latest financial disclosures, amid broader concerns over the ballooning cost of financing AI.
item.dc:creator: Milana Vinn, Anirban Sen
item.content:encoded: Some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors in its upcoming initial public offering are weighing a lower valuation for the AI company after its latest financial disclosures, four people familiar with the matter said, amid broader concerns over the ballooning cost of financing AI. Some investors who attended [USN:L6N4601AA TEXT:"Anthropic's investor day"] on Wednesday in San Francisco discussed a valuation of around $1.5 trillion, three of the people said, a significant step down from the roughly $2 trillion valuation that investors had previously expected for the November share sale. At Wednesday's meeting, Anthropic told prospective IPO investors that its third-quarter revenue jumped 45% to $16.8 billion from the previous quarter, and that it was profitable on an adjusted basis during the quarter. While those numbers assuaged some concerns about the massive costs of developing AI systems, some investors were disappointed by the slowing sequential growth rate in the latest quarter, as Anthropic's revenue more than doubled from the first quarter to $11.6 billion in the second quarter, the people added. They spoke on condition of anonymity because they are not authorized to speak publicly on the matter. Anthropic did not immediately respond to requests for comment. A cooler reception for Anthropic's IPO could weigh on the wider AI market, whose near-term prospects investors see as hinging largely on the share sale's success, followed by [USN:L6N45407M TEXT:"OpenAI's potential listing"] next year. BELLWETHER IPO The concerns from investors come as a tech selloff is roiling global financial markets and has hurt AI infrastructure companies, chipmakers and so-called neocloud providers that rent computing power for AI broadly. Shares and bonds of Nvidia (NVDA.O) -backed CoreWeave (CRWV.O) [USN:L4N46111C TEXT:" tumbled on Thursday"], reflecting growing investor concern about an AI buildout that is increasingly being financed with borrowed money. A disappointing share sale for Anthropic could further add to investor worries about the AI buildout. The IPO market has suffered [USN:L6N45H0SG TEXT:"some setbacks"] recently, after data center operator SB Energy decided to delay its listing last month, while nuclear technology company Holtec Nuclear [USN:L4N4581N0 TEXT:"pulled its plans to go public"]. During Wednesday's meeting at Anthropic's headquarters in San Francisco, attendees, mostly the company's most prominent investors, met with CEO Dario Amodei and finance chief Krishna Rao. The Information earlier reported that investors were considering a lower valuation. Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI executives including Amodei and his sister Daniela Amodei, who is now Anthropic's president, Anthropic has emerged as one of the leading generative AI developers with its Claude family of models. The company's rapid growth has been underpinned by Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) Google and Amazon (AMZN.O) , which are simultaneously investors, suppliers of computing power and important distribution partners, as well as AI competitors. Last year, Anthropic's revenue surged twelvefold to nearly $4.6 billion, even as the company lost more than $8 billion on an operating basis, excluding writedowns of various liabilities mostly tied to previous fundraising, Reuters [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"reported "]last month. In its IPO prospectus seen exclusively by Reuters in September, Anthropic laid out a vision that AI will transform the global economy more profoundly than industrialization, electricity and the internet, even as it reported a loss of $42 billion in 2025 and projected more spending for the upcoming AI buildout. The company has committed to spending [USN:L1N45K0RM TEXT:"at least $518 billion"] over a decade for cloud services, computing and infrastructure.

item.title: "Disgusting and despicable": Vance warns against selling White House access
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance on Thursday (local time) said anyone found selling access to the White House should face consequences, responding to questions about allegations involving former US ...
item.content:encoded:
"Disgusting and despicable": Vance warns against selling White House access US Vice President JD Vance on Thursday (local time) said anyone found selling access to the White House should face consequences, responding to questions about allegations involving former US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle and potential conflicts of interest in President Donald Trump's administration, CBS News reported. ANI | Updated: 16-10-2026 09:30 IST | Created: 16-10-2026 09:30 IST

US Vice President JD Vance (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US Vice President JD Vance on Thursday (local time) said anyone found selling access to the White House should face consequences, responding to questions about allegations involving former US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle and potential conflicts of interest in President Donald Trump's administration, CBS News reported. "First of all, if somebody's selling access to the White House, that's disgusting and despicable, and they should suffer consequences," Vance told CBS News. Speaking with 'CBS Evening News' anchor Tony Dokoupil during a town hall in Michigan, scheduled to air on Saturday, Vance said allegations should be assessed based on evidence. "I want to make those judgments based on the facts and not based on a random news media report that I read," he said. Dokoupil raised reports concerning Trump's cryptocurrency earnings and Guilfoyle's departure from her diplomatic post following allegations that she had asked a man seeking assistance from the Trump administration to wire her USD 100,000. Asked whether the administration would comply with congressional subpoenas if Democrats won control of the House of Representatives or the Senate in the midterm elections, Vance said, "Of course I will. Look, I mean, we follow the law." Earlier on Tuesday, Guilfoyle confirmed that she was leaving her post as US Ambassador to Greece after the White House asked her to resign. In a post on X, she denied the allegations and said, "I also want to address the recent allegations against me. These allegations are false, and I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity." White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia said Guilfoyle had been asked to leave her post. "She has been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well," Zacharia said. Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Trump distanced himself from Guilfoyle, saying she had previously dated his eldest son, Donald Trump Jr. "She wasn't a member of my family. She, I guess, dated my son a long time ago," Trump said, according to Fox News. He added, "She was doing a good job, but we didn't like what we were reading." The Wall Street Journal reported that Guilfoyle had asked Trump donor Eric Deters to pay a USD 100,000 American Express bill shortly before her Senate confirmation hearing in July 2025. Deters said he did not make the payment, while Guilfoyle's attorney, Jesse Binnall, disputed the authenticity of the messages cited in the report. Separately, financial disclosures released by the US Office of Government Ethics showed that Trump reported more than USD 1.4 billion in income from his family's cryptocurrency ventures in 2025, including more than USD 500 million from World Liberty Financial and USD 635 million from the sale of his $TRUMP meme coins. The reports have raised questions about potential conflicts of interest involving the President's business interests and his public office. Trump has denied any conflicts of interest. (ANI)

item.description: ［ニューヨーク １５日 ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場では、ドルが円やユーロなどの主要通貨に対し下落した。連邦準備...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ外為市場＝ドル下落、ＡＩ関連企業への懸念が重し　10月利上げ観測後退 5:53 配信

２０１１年１月撮影　REUTERS/Kacper Pempel

［ニューヨーク　１５日　ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場では、ドルが円やユーロなどの主要通貨に対し下落した。連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）当局者の慎重な発言を受け１０月の利上げ観測が後退しているほか、この日発表された堅調な物価・消費関連指標よりもＡＩ（人工知能）向けデータセンター関連企業を巡る懸念に市場の関心が集まったことがドルの重しになった。

この日発表の米経済指標では、９月の小売売上高が前月比０．８％増加。ガソリン価格の上昇を背景に予想を上回る伸びとなったが、ガソリン以外の支出は総じて緩やかで、自動車、ガソリン、建設資材、外食サービスを除くコア小売売上高は前月比０．１％増と、伸びは前月から鈍化した。

９月の卸売物価指数（ＰＰＩ、最終需要向け財・サービス）は前年比６．３％上昇。２０２２年１２月以来の大幅な伸びとなり、エネルギー関連以外にもインフレが広がっている可能性が改めて示された。

マネックスＵＳＡのトレーディング部門責任者、フアン・ペレス氏は「現在のインフレ率とその上昇ペースは持続不可能との見方から、ドルに弱気な相場観が広がっている」と指摘。「景気停滞を巡る懸念が市場心理に大きく影響する中、この４週間の大幅なドル高を受けて市場はドル売りに傾いている」と述べた。

前日に発表された９月の消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）は前年比は３．７％上昇と、伸びは前月の３．４％から加速。予想の３．６％も上回った。これを受け、当初はＦＲＢは追加利上げに動くとの見方が強まったものの、その後、ボウマンＦＲＢ副議長やサンフランシスコ地区連銀のデイリー総裁が判断材料を見極める時間的余裕があるとの認識を示したことで、利上げ観測は後退した。

ＣＭＥフェドウオッチによると、ＦＲＢが２７─２８日の会合で金利据え置きを決定する確率は７３％。１カ月前の５３％から上昇した。

ロンドンのＬＭＡＸグループで市場ストラテジストを務めるジョエル・クルーガー氏は、ＡＩ関連企業の多額の債務負担への懸念が再燃したことで安全資産とされる米国債に資金が流入していることに関連し、「国債利回りの上昇が続かず、ドル相場の上昇局面で売りが続く場合、インフレ関連の材料はおおむね市場に織り込まれたとの見方が強まる。その場合、リスク資産に有利な方向に市場のリスクバランスが傾く」と述べた。

市場ではＦＲＢの金融政策の行方を見極めようと、ウォーシュＦＲＢ議長が１６日にバンコクで開かれる国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）・世界銀行年次総会で行う講演が注目されている。

メシロー・カレンシー・マネジメントのシニア投資戦略担当者、ウト・シノハラ氏は「ＦＲＢはまもなく（ＦＯＭＣ前後に金融政策に関する発言を控える）ブラックアウト期間に入る上、ＦＯＭＣまでに重要な経済指標の発表は残されていない」とし、「このため、市場の方向性は引き続きロシア・ウクライナ情勢やイランを巡る地政学的な不透明感に加え、ＡＩを巡る動向に左右される可能性が高い」としている。

終盤の取引で主要通貨に対するドル指数は０．４５％安の１０１．９９。前日は１年６カ月ぶりの高値を付けていた。

ユーロは対ドルで０．５６％高の１．１２１８ドル。円は対ドルで０．１５％高の１５８．０８円。

item.title: Nova Scotia premier defends changing his stance on welcoming data centre proposals
item.description: Nova Scotia Premier Tim Houston is defending his decision to change his stance on when data centres might be considered for approval to operate in the province.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: HALIFAX — Nova Scotia Premier Tim Houston is defending his decision to change his stance on when data centres might be considered for approval to operate in the province. In June, the premier said it was too soon to turn his government’s attention to the matter, and that it would not be discussed until far into the future. A few months later, he softened that stance, opening a door to consider proposals from the sector. “A lot has happened … in the world, geopolitics, all kinds of situations there,” Houston told reporters Thursday. “When you look at some of the positioning of the federal government around data sovereignty, around the regulations that would be required, (they) definitely were thoughtful and had an impact on me.” The premier had previously said discussions about data centres would have to wait until the province had completed major energy generation projects, including the ambitious Wind West offshore wind farms. “We’re going to generate significant amounts of energy … (and) at that point in time, that would be a more appropriate discussion,” he said on June 18. At the time, the premier said the discussion about data centres “is so far out in the future … but there wouldn’t be a commitment to a data centre unless we could fully supply the energy without any risk to Nova Scotians.” Late last month, however, Houston said data centres are becoming increasingly critical pieces of infrastructure, adding that Canada can’t rely on other countries to store its data. He said he became more open to considering data centre proposals after Ottawa rolled out its new rules. “I think the sentiment of that (June) statement was that we wouldn’t allow an impact on ratepayers,” Houston said Thursday. “We’re not going to drive up the rates to let another user, any type of industrial use, have their power while households and Nova Scotians pay more. That sentiment remains.” Data centres, used in AI and other high-tech industries, are typically massive operations that require immense amounts of electricity to run and cool off computer servers. EverWind Fuels, the company planning a large-scale green hydrogen project in Cape Breton to be powered by onshore wind, says it’s exploring setting up a data centre at an existing industrial site at Point Tupper, N.S. The proposed data centre “would form part of the broader Point Tupper Energy Hub and complement EverWind’s clean energy projects across Nova Scotia,” company spokesperson Claire Parsons said in an email Thursday. Parsons declined to say if the proposed data centre would be used for artificial intelligence. Official Opposition Leader Claudia Chender called Houston’s changed stance on data centres a “stunning reversal.” “When the premier said not long ago that we were not considering AI data centres, not today, not tomorrow … people took him at his word as they watched these debates play out in other places,” Chender, the NDP leader, told reporters Thursday. Last month, Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew rejected plans for a massive AI data centre southeast of Winnipeg. Kinew said the project’s size, energy use and community impact outweighed its limited gains. He said he was also skeptical of the long-term demand for centres of this scale given advances in computing. Meanwhile, Bell Canada intends to quadruple the size of its planned data centre project in Saskatchewan, with Prime Minister Mark Carney saying last month the project is expected to bring in more than $50 billion in capital investment. Alberta has also embraced data centre development. Electricity generator TransAlta Corp. announced plans in February to power a new data centre west of Edmonton. This came after the provincial technology minister said in 2024 that province was hoping to see $100 billion worth of artificial intelligence data centres under construction over five years. Environmental advocates have raised concerns about the massive volume of energy and water used by data centres. They’ve also warned about the potential for chemical pollution. A recent United Nations University report says the environmental footprint of data centres globally already rivals some of the world’s largest countries. The report also predicts their water and energy use and pollution will double in just four years as use of artificial intelligence grows. Chender and interim Liberal leader Iain Rankin both said Thursday they have serious concerns about the potential environmental impacts and water use tied to a data centre. Houston said Thursday a data centre in Nova Scotia would have to go through an approval process that could exceed federal requirements. This means the process would need to consider the impact on the environment and ratepayers. Both opposition leaders said these protections should be built into legislation. “It’s one thing to say that water and environmental concerns and ratepayers will be protected, but it’s not a fact that the premier’s word is stronger than regulations or legislation,” Rankin said. This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 15, 2026. Lyndsay Armstrong, The Canadian Press

item.description:
Aditya Soni
[１５日 ロイター] - 米人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業のアンソロピックは１５日、ＡＩの安全性を...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
アンソロピック、外部評価機関ＭＥＴＲに社員並みアクセス　ＡＩ安全性強化へ 5:36 配信

米カリフォルニア州サンフランシスコで開催されたDreamforce 2026テクノロジーサミットで９月撮影。REUTERS/Carlos Barria

Aditya Soni

[１５日 ロイター] - 米人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業のアンソロピックは１５日、ＡＩの安全性を研究する非営利団体ＭＥＴＲに、自社システムへの社員レベルのアクセス権を付与したと明らかにした。ＡＩ新興企業ハギングフェイス など他の組織とも協議中という。ＡＩ各社は、技術開発のペースを遅らせることなく安全性を高める手段として、外部評価機関の活用を打ち出している。

アンソロピックはブログで、生物安全保障分野の非営利団体「セキュアバイオ」や、コンサルティング大手アクセンチュアのＡＩ事業部門ファカルティーも評価機関として起用していると説明した。

アンソロピックによると、ＭＥＴＲの職員６人には、同社のハードウエア、オフィススペースのほか、社内のリスク評価チームとほぼ同等の内部システムへのアクセス権が与えられる。ただし、顧客データ、法的機密情報、モデルのアーキテクチャーについてはアクセス対象外となる。

アンソロピックは、セキュアバイオやファカルティーなど他の評価機関との提携は初期段階にあり、アクセス権や公表権は限定的だと述べた。

item.title: Wall Street muscles higher despite more swings for AI stocks
item.description: A sell-off for artificial-intelligence stocks is hitting Wall Street again Thursday after whipping around the world on worries about how much longer the AI frenzy will last.
item.dc:creator: The Associated Press
item.content:encoded: NEW YORK — U.S. stock indexes muscled higher Thursday, led by companies delivering bigger profits. They pulled closer to their records even as stocks in the artificial intelligence industry kept swinging on worries about how much longer their boom will last. The S&P 500 rose 0.3 per cent after erasing an early-morning loss and pulled closer to its all-time high set last week. The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 556 points, or 1.1 per cent, while the Nasdaq composite added 0.1 per cent. Marsh & McLennan helped lead the way and rallied 4.6 per cent after the insurance and professional services firm that updated its brand name to Marsh reported a stronger profit for the summer than analysts expected. Expectations are high for growth in profits from all kinds of companies this reporting season, which began in earnest this week. That’s what’s allowed U.S. stocks to set records despite high inflation and the many other worries weighing on Wall Street. Kimberly-Clark climbed 4.7 per cent after the company behind Huggies, Kleenex and Kotex said it expects to report revenue and profit for the latest quarter above what analysts had been expecting. Bank of New York Mellon rose 3.2 per cent after reporting a stronger profit than analysts expected, and CEO Robin Vince said BNY saw strength across its regions. Markets had been much shakier earlier in the day. A sell-off for AI stocks that began on Wall Street Wednesday whipped around the world and sent South Korea’s Kospi stock index down 7.6 per cent and Japan’s Nikkei 225 down 4.9 per cent before knocking the S&P 500 lower at the start of Thursday’s trading. They’re the latest jarring moves for AI stocks after they led the market for years. Companies are pouring money into the technology in hopes of bigger profits and improved productivity. But data centers and AI chips cost money, and many companies have been borrowing the cash to get them. Now, after yields in bond markets worldwide hit their highest levels in years and made borrowing money more expensive, worries are rising about how resilient that boom in spending can be. High yields in the bond market also generally make investors less willing to pay high prices for stocks, particularly those seen as the most expensive. Nvidia, the chip company that’s ridden the AI boom to become Wall Street’s most valuable company, fell 1.8 per cent and was the heaviest weight on the S&P 500. It came into the day with a nearly 1,415 per cent gain since the end of 2022. But the losses for AI stocks moderated as the day progressed, which helped broad U.S. indexes to steady. Nvidia more than halved an early-morning loss that had reached 3.8 per cent. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. ’s stock that trades in the United States dropped as much as 5.3 per cent in the morning before finishing with a more modest loss of 1.8 per cent. The bellwether for the AI industry reported a profit for the latest quarter that topped analysts’ high expectations, and Chief Financial Officer Wendell Huang said it expects strong demand to continue in the final three months of 2026. CoreWeave, which offers AI computing power to customers over the cloud, fell as much as 9.5 per cent in the morning after tumbling 15.5 per cent a day earlier. It later flipped to a gain and finished 5.9 per cent higher. All told, the S&P 500 rose 25.12 points to 7,744.06. The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 556.21 to 52,177.69, and the Nasdaq composite added 20.16 to 26,713.03. In the bond market, Treasury yields fell, which means investors were willing to pay higher prices to buy U.S. government bonds. Treasurys have a reputation as a safer investment, and investors often flock to them when feeling nervous. The yield on the 10-year Treasury sank to 5.09 per cent from 5.19 per cent late Wednesday. It had topped 5.30 per cent earlier this month and touched its highest level since 2002 because of worries about high inflation, signals of a strong U.S. economy and other factors. The drop in yields came even though another report signaled inflation has worsened in the United States by more than economists expected. Several reports on the U.S. economy also came in stronger than economists expected, which typically pushes yields upward. One report said U.S. retailers made more money last month than economists expected, while another said fewer U.S. workers applied for unemployment benefits last week than expected. In stock markets abroad, South Korea’s loss was the headliner. Its Kospi index is dominated by two chip companies, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, and it fell to its worst day since July. It has dropped 39 per cent since setting a record in June. Indexes were stronger in Europe, which has less of a dependence on tech stocks. London’s FTSE 100 rallied 1.1 per cent for one of the world’s biggest gains. ___ Stan Choe, The Associated Press AP Business Writers Chan Ho-him and Matt Ott contributed to this report.

Oct 15 : Thoma Bravo-owned cybersecurity company Proofpoint will buy data security firm Varonis Systems in an all-cash deal valued at about $6.3 billion, the companies said on Thursday. Under the agreement, Varonis shareholders will receive $49.75 per share in cash, a 52 per cent premium to the company's closing share price on June 22, the day before speculation about a possible sale first emerged, the companies said.  The offer values Varonis' equity at $5.71 billion. Its shares rose about 2.7 per cent in extended trading. The deal, expected to close in the first half of 2027, comes as businesses ramp up spending on cybersecurity to combat cybercrime, where AI is being increasingly used to steal data.

Miami-based Varonis offers digital security services, including data classification on cloud storage systems and employee behavior tracking. "Our mission is to secure AI and the data that powers it. By joining forces with Proofpoint, we can achieve this mission faster than ever," Varonis co-founder and CEO Yaki Faitelson said. Reuters had reported in September that Proofpoint was in discussions to acquire Varonis Systems. In June, media outlets had reported that Varonis was weighing a sale after fielding takeover interest from private equity firms, sending the company's shares surging about 30 per cent. Proofpoint, which sells software that helps companies defend against cyberattacks, was bought by Thoma Bravo in 2021 in a take-private deal that valued the company at about $12.3 billion. Goldman Sachs & Co was the financial advisor to Varonis, while BofA Securities, Morgan Stanley & Co, J.P. Morgan Securities, UBS Securities, and Mizuho Securities USA advised Proofpoint. Varonis said it will announce its financial results for the third quarter on November 3, but will not hold an earnings conference call.

item.title: Canadian artificial intelligence company Cohere to buy Aisle
item.description: Canadian artificial intelligence firm Cohere says it has signed a letter of intent to purchase a cybersecurity business.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: TORONTO — Canadian artificial intelligence firm Cohere says it has signed a letter of intent to purchase a cybersecurity business. Cohere’s acquisition target is Aisle, a company split between San Francisco and Prague that has developed AI systems capable of uncovering and remediating vulnerabilities in software. Cohere did not immediately reveal the value or structure of the deal, as well as its expected closing date. Cohere framed the proposed transaction as a way to further develop sovereign AI and invest in Europe, the home of its recent acquisitions Aleph Alpha and Reliant AI. Aisle was started last year by Ondrej Vlcek, the ex-chief executive of Avast, a Czech antivirus provider. Vlcek and his two fellow co-founders will take on leadership roles at Cohere, which has promised to make a substantial long-term investment in Prague to further expand Aisle. --- Tara Deschamps, The Canadian Press This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 15, 2025.

item.description: Oct 15 : CoreWeave's mounting debt is raising fresh concerns about the AI boom, as investors question whether demand can justify the billions being borrowed to build data centres.Shares and bonds of the Nvidia-backed company have tumbled despite its CEO's assurances of a strong contract backlog, fueling a bro

Explainer-Why CoreWeave's troubles are rattling the AI boom

FAST

Oct 15 : CoreWeave's mounting debt is raising fresh concerns about the AI boom, as investors question whether demand can justify the billions being borrowed to build data centres. Shares and bonds of the Nvidia-backed company have tumbled despite its CEO's assurances of a strong contract backlog, fueling a broader selloff in technology stocks. Here is why investors are worried and what its troubles could mean for the industry. WHAT DOES COREWEAVE DO?

CoreWeave rents out computing power from Nvidia processors to companies developing and running AI, including Microsoft and OpenAI. It is one of the leading "neocloud" providers, a group of newer cloud companies that are growing rapidly to meet demand for scarce and expensive AI chips. These neocloud companies give customers access to computing power without requiring them to build their own data centers. However, supplying such capacity requires heavy upfront investment in chips and infrastructure, often financed with debt. WHAT IS ITS FINANCIAL SITUATION? The company, which has never turned a profit, has about $50 billion in debt, according to data compiled by LSEG. It raised its annual capital spending forecast by $4 billion in August to between $35 billion and $39 billion. Analysts expect revenue of nearly $13 billion this year and a loss of $2.13 billion. The yields on its bonds due in 2031, which are rated junk, have spiked to about 16 per cent, while the cost of insuring its debt against default has climbed to about 1,000 basis points, reflecting growing concern among creditors. CEO Mike Intrator told employees in an internal memo seen by Reuters that its deal backlog more than covers its debt obligations. The company had a $104.2 billion revenue backlog at the end of the second quarter, followed by more than $25 billion in new commitments early in the third quarter. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has also downplayed the concerns, saying CoreWeave's financial strength is improving and he sees no need to backstop it. The chip giant has agreed to buy unsold CoreWeave capacity through April 2032. WHY IT COULD BE A CANARY IN THE COAL MINE CoreWeave's business depends on two things: demand for AI computing and lenders' willingness to finance the infrastructure supplying it. But a selloff in its shares suggests a lack of confidence among investors in the latter, even as the company cites strong demand. The concern is not that AI demand will collapse, but that higher borrowing costs could make the business harder to sustain if demand were to weaken sharply. "It looks more like investors questioning how the build-out is being funded than a sudden collapse in appetite for AI computing," said Axel Rudolph, chief technical analyst at IG Group. "CoreWeave is quickly becoming the AI trade's canary in the coal mine," said Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB. WHY ARE MARKETS FRETTING? Investors are questioning whether AI revenue can grow fast enough to cover the cost of building and financing the infrastructure. CoreWeave has to spend heavily upfront before it can collect the revenue from its contracts. Higher interest rates could drive up financing costs and further squeeze returns. The hardware itself poses another risk. Chips lose value as newer generations arrive, pushing providers to spend even more to replace them. The concerns, however, go beyond CoreWeave. US technology giants are expected to spend more than $700 billion on AI infrastructure this year. THE DOWNSIDE SCENARIO One potential consequence would be a broader financing squeeze, with lenders demanding higher returns or becoming less willing to fund other AI projects. That could force providers to scale back expansion, curbing equipment purchases and affecting the computing capacity customers expect. A setback could also deepen doubts that the AI investment frenzy is outpacing returns, piling further pressure on technology stocks. The impact of the fallout would depend on how the business is reorganized, and CoreWeave's ties to major technology companies do not, by themselves, mean its failure would trigger a wider financial crisis. WHO ELSE BEARS THE RISK? Gartner estimates about 80 per cent of neoclouds could shut down by 2030, warning that expected AI revenue will not support profitable returns on all planned infrastructure spending. Neocloud rivals Nebius, Applied Digital and Iren have fallen in the recent selloff. The cost of default protection has risen for SoftBank, which is betting heavily on OpenAI. Meanwhile, spreads for Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Nvidia have also reached records, although they have risen much more slowly than CoreWeave's. However, these companies also have larger cash flows and stronger balance sheets.

Source: Reuters

item.content:encoded:
Home / Markets / Commodities / Oil prices dip but head for weekly gains amid West Asia supply concerns

Oil prices dip but head for weekly gains amid West Asia supply concerns The International Energy Agency agreed to release over 20 million barrels of diesel to the market and any oil remaining from a record release of emergency reserves pledged in March to boost supply

For this week so far, Brent has increased 0.72 per cent, while WTI has jumped 5.9 per cent

Reuters BEIJING 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 16 2026 | 1:50 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Oil prices eased on Friday but were heading for weekly gains on uncertainty over Middle East supplies and a larger-than-expected draw from US crude stockpiles, while European diesel margins dropped following the IEA's decision to release more diesel.   Brent crude futures were down 47 cents, or 0.44 per cent, at $105.45 a barrel by 0747 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down 62 cents, or 0.63 per cent, to $97.35.   WTI settled up more than 3 per cent on Thursday after a big US crude stock draw on hurricane production shut-ins.   For this week so far, Brent has increased 0.72 per cent, while WTI has jumped 5.9 per cent.

"Uncertainty in the Middle East and concerns over the sustainability of oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz has the market pricing in a significant risk premium," ING analysts wrote in a note. Also Read

West Asia war keeps $110 in sight for oil despite supply recovery: Analyst

Oil prices rise as traders weigh Saudi supply risk, Russian diesel flow

Oil volatility to rise ahead of midterm; Brent may test $120: Analyst

Record FPI outflows top ₹3 trillion in CY26, nearly double 2025 tally

Houthis used Claude to develop missiles, test-fired rocket: Anthropic

Some kind of agreement between the US and Iran was required to provide more confidence to the market that stronger oil flows from the region would continue, they added. Iran says it is stepping up strikes near the Strait of Hormuz Supply jitters also increased as attacks around the Strait of Hormuz surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it was stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month.

Total Hormuz clearance averaged 11.62 million barrels per day over the seven days to October 13, about 68 per cent of the 17.15 million bpd baseline, said ship tracking firm Kpler.   European diesel refining margins declined by nearly 2 per cent on Friday to $78.67 a barrel, after the International Energy Agency agreed on Thursday to release over 20 million barrels of diesel to the market.   Those margins rose as high as $95 a barrel in September as diesel supply tightened because of wars in Ukraine and Iran.   "Intensified Iranian attacks drove Gulf crude flows sharply lower," Kpler analysts said in a report on Thursday, adding that they expected a slower and more uneven Hormuz recovery in the absence of a comprehensive political deal.

The Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing two guards, while the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen detailed dozens of attacks on Saudi infrastructure in the escalating conflict.   The Trump administration is considering lifting sanctions on some so-called shadow fleet vessels that have carried oil and petroleum products from countries such as Russia, Iran and Venezuela, in a bid to cut record global freight rates, a US official said on Wednesday.   The discussions come days after President Donald Trump temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian diesel fuel, a move met with criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, European countries and some of Trump's fellow Republicans.

item.title: Rio Tinto prevé que las lluvias en Argentina afecten a la producción de litio
item.description: El Grupo Rio Tinto ha indicado que la producción de litio para todo el año se situará en el extremo inferior de las previsiones, después de que las condiciones meteorológicas afectaran a sus operacion ...
item.dc:creator: Paul-Alain Hunt, Katharine Gemmell, Annie Lee
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — El Grupo Rio Tinto ha indicado que la producción de litio para todo el año se situará en el extremo inferior de las previsiones, después de que las condiciones meteorológicas afectaran a sus operaciones en Argentina. El proyecto de Olaroz producirá menos de este metal para baterías a partir de los estanques de salmuera debido a las precipitaciones, mientras que su explotación de Fénix también se ha visto afectada, según indicó Rio Tinto en su informe del tercer trimestre publicado este miércoles. El avance de su proyecto de salmuera en construcción, “Sal de Vida”, también ha sido más lento de lo previsto. El litio se obtiene normalmente mediante la evaporación de salmuera o la extracción de rocas duras. VER MÁS: Rio Tinto consigue su segundo RIGI: invertirá US$530 millones en un proyecto de litio Rio Tinto es la única gran empresa minera diversificada que cuenta con activos de litio, tras adquirir un importante productor en 2024. El mercado se ha mostrado volátil en los últimos años debido a las cambiantes expectativas en torno a los vehículos eléctricos y los sistemas de almacenamiento de energía, así como a las incertidumbres en el suministro en centros de producción como China y Zimbabue. Los precios han retrocedido en las últimas semanas ante la creciente preocupación por la demanda, y Goldman Sachs Group ha pronosticado este mes que se producirá un excedente en los próximos dos años. La producción equivalente de carbonato de litio rondará las 61.000 toneladas en el ejercicio que finaliza el 31 de diciembre, según ha indicado la segunda mayor empresa minera del mundo. Las previsiones tanto para la producción de cobre como para las ventas de mineral de hierro se mantuvieron sin cambios. La producción de cobre se mantuvo estable en el tercer trimestre, ya que los buenos resultados de su mina de Mongolia compensaron los descensos registrados en otros lugares, mientras que los envíos de mineral de hierro aumentaron ligeramente. El cobre, que representó más de un tercio de los ingresos de la empresa minera en el primer semestre del año, es una parte fundamental de los planes del grupo para aprovechar la creciente demanda de electrificación derivada de la transición energética y de los centros de datos. La producción durante los tres meses que finalizaron en septiembre fue de 205 000 toneladas. VER MÁS: Lithium Argentina mejora sus resultados, proyecta invertir US$4.500 millones y sumar un socio La producción de su mina de Escondida, en Chile, descendió debido a la menor ley del mineral, un breve cierre y las adversas condiciones meteorológicas, según informó Rio Tinto. Esto se vio compensado por un aumento en la mina de Oyu Tolgoi, en Mongolia, donde la empresa minera está ampliando sus operaciones subterráneas. Las ventas de mineral de hierro —ingrediente clave para la fabricación de acero y la mayor fuente de ingresos de Rio Tinto— aumentaron un 3% con respecto al año anterior, hasta alcanzar los 90,8 millones de toneladas en el tercer trimestre. La empresa sigue aumentando la producción en su mina de SimFer, que forma parte del proyecto Simandou en Guinea, mientras que la producción de sus principales minas de mineral de hierro australianas se mantuvo estable. Rio Tinto también se encuentra ultimando un acuerdo de suministro con el comprador de mineral de hierro respaldado por el Estado chino. China Mineral Resources Group Co., creada para negociar en nombre de la industria siderúrgica, indicó a algunas acerías a principios de septiembre que aplazaran las compras de la mezcla “Pilbara Blend” de la empresa minera, ya que las negociaciones del contrato habían llegado a un punto crítico. Las negociaciones con CMRG han supuesto un quebradero de cabeza para las empresas del sector, entre ellas Fortescue Ltd. y BHP Group. --Con la colaboración de Katharine Gemmell y Annie Lee. Germany warns against bringing Russia back into G20 fold

At a G20 finance ministers’ meeting in Bangkok, German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said, “There will be no pretending that Russia is now returning as a normal member of the G20 and simply taking its seat at the table again - not with me, and not with the other Europeans.”

German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil speaks during the annual review meeting of the "Made for Germany" initiative, at Siemens AG in Berlin, Germany Sep 30, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Annegret Hilse)

FAST

BANGKOK: Germany warned on Thursday (Oct 15) against efforts to bring Russia back on to the international stage, while Britain called for tighter sanctions on Russia n shipping, as questions grow about the strength of US support for Ukraine. Russia n Finance Minister Anton Siluanov attended a meeting of G20 finance ministers and central bankers in Bangkok, just over a month after the US had hosted his first in-person G20 appearance since Russia invaded Ukraine, at a meeting in Asheville, North Carolina. "I do notice attempts, particularly from the United States ... to bring Russia back onto the international stage," German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil told reporters. "There will be no pretending that Russia is now returning as a normal member of the G20 and simply taking its seat at the table again - not with me, and not with the other Europeans."

RIFT OVER RUSSIA SANCTIONS US Treasury Undersecretary Erin Browne said Washington supported Russia's presence, noting that allies had not raised their concerns directly with the US delegation this week. "We think it's really important if you're going to solve a crisis, you need to have open dialogue and open conversation," she told Reuters. "And you can't have ... dialogue, and you can't have resolution to conflict if no one's talking to one another." US President Donald Trump remained committed to bringing about a peaceful end to the war between Russia and Ukraine, she said. British finance minister John Healey called on other nations to tighten sanctions on Russia -linked shipping. "My message to finance ministers here today ... on Ukraine, is to stay the path on tough economic sanctions on Russia , especially a tighter ban on shipping services ... that help ( Russia n President Vladimir) Putin's sanctions-busting shadow fleet to operate," he said. Britain has imposed a series of sanctions on shipping and related services that it believes Russia uses to fund and equip its war on Ukraine.

Related:

Commentary: Trump’s Russian diesel U-turn comes at bad time for Ukraine
